(2) The University shall restrict to phase-wise development of its academic
programmers and having developed the necessary infrastructure it shall
launch its academic programmers subsequently.
(3) The University may associate external examiners for the conduct of
examinations.
(4) No degree shall be granted unless a student has passed an examination
in Islamic and Pakistan studies at the Bachelor's degree level or, in the
case of a non-Muslim student, in Ethics and Pakistan Studies at his
option.

7. Authorities of the University. - The following shall be the Authorities of the
University:-
(a) the Academic Council;
(b) the Advanced Studies and Research Board;
(c) the Board;
(d) the Board of Faculty / Board of Studies;
(e) the Selection Board; and
(f) such other Authorities as may be specified by regulations to be the
Authority.
8. Officers of the University. The following shall be the officers of the
University, namely:
(a) the Chancellor;
(b) the Rector;
(c) the Deans;

7
(d) the Directors;
(e) the Registrar;
(f) the Treasurer;
(g) the Controller Examination;
(h) Such other persons as may be specified by regulations to be the
officers;

9. Patron. - (1) The Governor of Balochistan shall be the Patron of the
University.
(2). The Patron or his nominee shall preside at the
convocation of the University.
(3) Every Proposal to confer an honorary degree shall be
subject to confirmation by the Patron.

10. Visitation. - (1) The Patron may cause a visitation or inquiry to be
made inrespect of any matter connected with the
affairs of the institute and appoint any such person as
he may deem fit for the purpose.
(2) The Patron may, on receipt of a report, issue such
directions as he thinks fit and the Chancellor shall
comply with such directions.

11. Chancellor.- (1) The President of society shall be the Chancellor of
the University.
(2) The Chancellor shall appoint a Rector.
(3) The Chancellor shall have the power to assent to
such rules and regulations as required to be
submitted to him by the society or withhold assent
or refer them back to the society for
reconsideration.
(4) In case the Chancellor is satisfied that the
proceedings of any Authority or order of any officer
are not in accordance with the provisions of this
Act, the rules or regulations, he may, after calling
upon such Authority or officer to show cause as to
why such proceedings or, as the case may be,
order should not be annulled, by order in writing,
annul such proceedings or orders.
12. Rector. -
(1) Rector shall be an eminent scholar of repute who shall be appointed by
the Chancellor.
(2) The Rector shall be the chief academic and administrative officer of the
University and shall be responsible for the implementation of the decisions
of the Board and for the execution of the programmes of the University in
accordance with the guidelines and policies formulated by the Board.
(3) The Rector shall-
(a) submit plans of work and budget estimates of the University for the
consideration of the Board;
(b) direct the activities connected with the execution of programmes for
instruction, training, research, demonstration, services to community.
etc;
(C) authorize expenditure provided for in the approved budget;

10
one eminent scholar and an educationist to be nominated by the
chancellor;
(k) four persons, prominent in the field of their specialization because of
their experience and achievements, to be nominated by the Society;
(I) Registrar of the University, who shall be the secretary;

(2) A nominated member of the Board shall hold office for a term of three
years and shall be eligible for re-nomination on the expiry of his term.
(3) The office of a nominated member of the Board shall become vacant if he
resigns or fails to attend three consecutive meetings of the Board with
sufficient case or leave of absence.
(4) A casual vacancy in the office of a member of the Board shall be filled by
a person nominated by the Authority which nominates the member whose
vacancy is to be filled.
(5) No Act or proceedings of the Board shall be invalid by reason only of the
existence of a vacancy in or a defect in the constitution of the Board.

14. Powers and functions of the Board. -
(1) The Board shall exercise the power and perform the following functions,
namely:--
(a) to hold, control and administer the property, funds, assets and
resources of the University;
(b) to transfer and accept transfer of movable or immovable property on
behalf of the University;
(c) to consider and approve, on the advice of the Finance and Planning
Committee, the annual and revised budget estimates and to lay down
guidelines or rules of business dealing with financial matters;
(d) to approve, carry out, vary or cancel contracts on behalf of the
University.
(e) to initiate and approve schemes for achievement of the objectives of
the University;

11
(f) to determine the form. and regulate the custody and use of common
seal of the University:
(g) to create professional, research, administrative posts and such other
posts as may be required to carry out for the purposes of the
University, and to suspend or abolish such posts;
(h) to take all such initiatives as it may consider necessary or desirable for
the efficient and effective management and functioning of the
University;
(i) to suspend, punish and remove from service, employees of the
University in the manner as may be prescribed after due enquiry and
defense;
to approve regulations on the recommendations of the appropriate
bodies: and
(k) to determine and administer all other matters concerning the
University.
(2) The Board may delegate any of its powers to the Rector subject to such
conditions as it may deem fit to impose.

15. Meetings of the Board.-
(1) The Board shall meet, at least twice in a year on such dates as may be
fixed by the Chancellor.
(2) Special meeting may be called at any time once in a year by and on the
direction of the Chancellor or on a request by not less than five members
of the Board to consider any matter of urgent nature.
(3) In the case of special meeting not less than ten clear days notice.shall be
given to the members of the Board and the agenda of the meeting shall be
restricted to the matter for which the special meeting is called.
(4) The quorum for a meeting of the Board shall be on half of its members, a
fraction being counted as one.

12
(5) The decision of the Board shall be expressed in terms of the views of the
majority of. the members present and voting and, if the members are
equally divided, the Chairman of the Board shall have a casting vote.

16. Director.
(1) The Board may appoint a Director of each campus of the Institute, on such
terms and conditions, as it may determine.
(2) The Director of a campus shall have the following powers, namely:-
(a) to sanction all expenditure provided for in the approved budget;
(b) to sanction reappropriation of an amount not exceeding such amount
as the Board may. authorize in this behalf for an unforeseen item not
provided for in the budget:
(c) to make such arrangements for the scrutiny of papers, markers and
results as may be necessary; and
(d) to direct teachers. officers and other employees of the campus of the
Institute to take up such assignments in connection with teaching,
research, examination, administration and such other activities in the
campus, as he may consider necessary.

17. Academic Council. -
(1) The Academic Council shall consist of-
(a) the Rector who shall be its Chairman;
(b) all Deans;
(c) the Directors of the respective campuses;
(d) the Heads of the Teaching Departments;
(e) the Controller Examination;
(f) all Professors of the University: and
(g) the Registrar who shall be the Secretary; and
(2) Members appointed by nomination shall hold office for three year and
shall be eligible for renomination.

13
(3) The quorum for a meeting of the Academic Council shall be one half of the
total number of its members, a fraction being counted as one.

18. Powers of the Academic Council.-
(1) The Academic Council shall be the academic body of the University and
shall, subject to the provisions of this Act and the Statutes, have the
powers to lay down proper standards of instructions, research,
publications and examinations and to regulate and promote the academic
standard of the University.
(2) In particular and without prejudice to the generality of the foregoing
provisions, and the Statutes, the Academic Council shall have the
powers-
(a) to advise the Board on academic matters;
(b) to regulate the çonduct of teaching, research, publications and
examinations;
(c) to regulate the admission of students to the courses of studies and
examination in the University:
(d) to regulate the conduct and discipline of the students of the University:
(e) to propose to the Board schemes for the constitution and organization
of faculties and teaching departments;
(f) to consider or formulate proposals for the planning and development of
teaching and research in the University:
(g) to make regulations prescribing the courses of studies; the syllabi and
the outlines of tests for all University examinations subject to the
approval of the Board;
(h) to regulate the award of fellowships, scholarships. stipends, bursaries,
exhibitions, medals and prizes;
(i) to frame regulations for submissions to the Board;
() to appoint or nominate members to the various authorities in
accordance with the provisions of this Act: and
(k) to perform such other functions as may be prescribed by statutes

14
'9 Constitutions, functions and powers of authorities. - Subject to the
provisions of this Act, the constitution, functions and the powers of the
authorities for which no specific provision has been made in this Act shall be
such as may be prescribed by Statutes.
20. Committees.-The Board, the Academic Council and any other authorities
may, from time to time, appoint such standing, special or advisory committees
as they may deem fit and may appoint such persons on these committees
who are not members of the authorities appointing the committees.
21. Indemnity.
(1) No suit, prosecution or legal proceedings shali lie against the University,
Board, any Authority or an employee of the University for anything, which
is done, or intended to be done in good faith under this Act.
(2) No decision taken, or thing done, by the Chancellor or the Board shall be
called in question before any court or other authority.

22. Power to make rules.
(1) Subject to the provisions of this Act, the Board may make rules for
carrying out the purposes of this Act.
(2) Without prejudice to the generality of the foregoing powers, such rules
may provide for-
(a) terms and conditions of contractual appointments of teachers,
researchers and officers;
(b) powers and duties of officers and teachers;
(C) conditions under which the University may enter into arrangements
with other public or private organizations for purposes of instructions,
research and other scholarly activities;
(d) conditions of appointment of Emeritus Professors and award of
honorary degrees;
(e) efficiency and discipline of the employees of the University;

15
(f) acquisition and administration of properties and investments in the
fund of the University; and
(g) all other matters which under this Act are required to be regulated by
rules.
(3) The Rector. the Director. the Deans or the Academic Council may propose
the draft of the rules of the Board.
(4) Any Authority or body of the University may propose rules. consistent with
the provisions of this Act, for approval of the Board. to regulate the
conduct of its business.

23. Statutes. -
(1) Subject to the provisions of this Act, Statutes may be made to regulate or
prescribe all or any of the following matters, namely:- -
(a) creation of Faculties. Teaching Departments and other Academic Units
and Divisions;
(b) service, pension and fringe benefits for University employees and
terms and conditions of their service;
(c) efficiency and discipline of the University employees; and
(d) all matters required to be regulate under the statues.
(2) The Board shall propose draft of the Statutes for approval by the Society
which may approve them, or refer them back for reconsideration, and no
statue shall be valid until the Society has approved it.
(3) Notwithstanding anything contained in sub-section (2). the Statutes set out
in the Schedule to this Act shall be deemed to be the Statutes framed
under this section and shall rervain in force until they are rescinded or
replaced by new Statues framed in accordance with this Act.

24. Removal of difficulties. 1
(1) If any difficulty arises in giving effect to any of the provisions of this Act,
the Chancellor may make such order, not in consistent with the provision

16
of this Act, as may appear to him to be necessary for removing the
difficulty.
(2) Where this Act makes any provision for anything to be done. but no
provision or no sufficient provision has been made as respects the
authority of whom. or the time at which. or the manner in which, it should
be done. then it shall be done by such authority, at such time, or in such
manner as the Chancellor may direct.

THE SCHEDULE
1. Faculties. - There shall be a faculty for a teaching department or a group of
teaching departments. The University shall include the following faculties and
such other faculties as may be prescribed by the Board.
(a) Faculty of Islam.
(b) Faculty of Science.
(c) Faculty of Arts.
(d) Faculty of Engineering; and
(e) Such other Faculty as may be prescribe by the statutes
2. Board of Facuityl Board of Studies.-
(1) There shall be a Board of each faculty which shall consist of -
(a) the Dean:
(b) the Professors and the Head of the teaching department in the Faculty;
(c) one member other than Professors and Head of each teaching
department to be nominated by the Head of Department;
(d) two teachers to be nominated by the Academic Council by reason of
their specialized knowledge of the subjects which, though not assigned
to the Faculty, have in the opinion of the Academic Council, important
bearing on the subjects assigned to the Faculty;
(e) two experts in the field from outside the University to be appointed by
the Board; and
(f) one member to be nominated by the Rector.

17
(2) The members, other than ex-officio members, shall hold office for three
years.
(3) The quorum for a meeting of the Board of a Faculty shall be one-half of
the total number of members, a fraction being counted as one.

3. Functions of the Board of Faculty.-The Board of each Faculty shall,
subject to the general control of the Academic Council and the Board, have
the powers to -
(a) co-ordinate the teaching, and research work in the subjects assigned
to the Faculty;
(b) scrutinise the recommendations of the Board of Studies, comprising
the Faculty with regard to the appointment of paper-setters and
examiner for graduate and post graduate examinations and to forward
the panels of suitable paper-setters and examiners for each
examination to the Rector;
(c) consider any other academic matter relating to the Faculty and report
thereon to the Academic Council:
(d) prepare a comprehensive annual report regarding the performance of
each department, comprising the Faculty for presentation to the
Academic Councit; and
(e) perform such other functions as may be prescribed by Statutes.

4. Dean.
(1) There shall be a Dean of each Faculty who shail be the Chairperson and
convener of the Board of Faculty.
(2) The Dean shall be appointed by the Board on the recommendation of
Rector from amongst the three most. senior Professors or Associate
Professor or any other person deem fit for the purpose and shall hold
office for a period up to three years and shall be eligible for re-
appointment.

18
(3) The Dean shall present candidates for admission. to degree (except
honorary degrees) in the courses falling within the purview of the Faculty.
(4) The Dean shall have such powers and duties as may be prescribed by the
Board on the recommendations of the Rector.

5. Academic Departments and Head of Departments.-
(1) There shall be an academic department for each subject or a group of
subjects as may be prescribed by Regulations and a Head of department
shall head each academic department.
(2) The Head of an academic department shall be appointed by the Board on
the recommendations of the Rector from amongst three senior most
Professors or Associate Professor other than Professor any other person
deem fit for the purpose and shall hold office for a period up to three years
and shall be eligible for re-appointment:
Provided that in a department in which there is no Professor or
Associate Professors - the appointment shall be made from amongst the
three senior most Associate Professors and Assistant Professors of the
department, beside it shall be look after by the Dean of the Faculty with
the assistance of the senior most teacher of the department.

(3) The Head of department shall plan, organize and supervise the work of
the department and shall be responsible to the Dean for the work of his
department.
(4) The Head of department shall, under the general supervision of the Rector
and the Dean, exercise all administrative, financial and academic powers
and such other duties or powers as may be delegated to him.
(5) The Head of department shall prepare a comprehensive annual report
regarding the performance of department at the graduate and
postgraduate levels, Faculty research and development and submit this
report to the Dean of the Faculty for his evaluation.

19
6. Board of Advanced Studies and Research. I -
(a) the Rector who shall be its Chairperson;
(b) all the Deans;
(C) one University professor from each faculty other than Professors
having experience in research in relevant field to be appointed by the
Academic Council;
(d) one University professor from each faculty other than Dean to be
appointed by the Board;
(e) one member to be nominated by the Rector;
(f) three members from the relevant field Research Organizations and
government departments to be nominated by the Board; and à
(g) the Registrar as Secretary.
(2: The team of office of the members of the Board of Advanced Studies and
Research, other than ex-officio members, shall be three years.
(3) The quorum for a meeting of the Board of Advanced Studies and
Research, shall be one-half of the total number of members, a fraction
being counted as one.
7. Functions of Board of Advanced Studies and Research. - The functions
of the Board of Advanced Studies and Research shall be to-
(a) advise the Authorities on all matters connected with the promotion of
advanced studies and research publication in the University;
(b) consider and report to the Authorities on the institution of research
degrees in the University;
(c) propose regulations regarding the award of research degrees;
(d) appoint supervisors for postgraduate research students and to approve
titles and synopses of their theses or dissertations.
(e) recommend panels of names of examiners for evaluation of their other
research examinations; and
(f) perform such other functions as may be prescribed by Statues.

20
8. Selection Board.-
(1) The Selection Board shall consist of -
(a) the Rector who shall be its Chairperson;
(b) the Dean of the Faculty concerned;
(c) the Head of the teaching department concerned;
(d) one member of the Board to be nominated by the Board;
(e) one eminent scientist or scholar to be nominated by the Society; and
- (f) one expert in the subject to be nominated by the University Grants
Commission;
(2) The Registrar shall be the Secretary of the Selection Board.
(3) The members, other than ex-officio members, shall hold office for three
year.
(4) The quorum for a meeting of the Selection Board shall be four.
(5) No member who is a candidate for the post to which appointment is to be
made shall take part in the proceedings of the Selection Board.
(6) The selection of candidate for the posts of Professors and Associate
Professors, the Selection Board shall co-opt or consult three experts in the
subject concerned. to be nominated by the Rector, from a standing list of
experts for each subject approved by the Board on the recommendations
of the Selection Board and revised from time to time.

9. Functions of the Selection Board. = The functions of the Selection Board
shall be-
(a) to consider the applications and recommend to the Board the names of
suitable candidates for appointment to teaching and other posts, as the
case may be, and recommend suitable salary for the person
concerned:
(b) to consider all cases of promotions or selection of officers of the
University and recommend the names of suitable candidates for such
promotion or selection the Board;

22
(c) two Professors or two Directors to be nominated by the Academic
Council.
(2) The term of office of the member of the Affiliation Committee other than
ex-officio members shall be two years.
(3) The Affiliation Committee may co-opt not more than three experts.
(4). The quorum of the meeting of the Affiliation Committee shall be three
members.
(5) An officer of the Institute to be designated by the Rector for this purpose
shall be the Secretary of the Affiliation Committee.

13. Discipline Committee.-
(1) The Discipline Committee shall consist of-
(a) the Rector or his nominee;
(b) two Professors to be nominated by the Academic Council;
(c) one member to be nominated by the Board; and
(d) the teacher or officer incharge Students Affairs by whatever name
called who shall be the member and Secretary.
(2) The term of office of the members of the Discipline Committee other than
ex-officio members shall be two years.
(3) The quorum for a meeting of the Discipline Committee shall be three
members.
(4) The functions of the Discipline Committee shall be
(a) to propose regulations to the Academic Council for the conduct of
University students, maintenance of discipline and for dealing with
cases of indiscipline; and

23
(b) to perform such other functions as may be assigned to it by
regulations.

Muhammad Khan Mengal,
Secretary,
Provincial Assembly of Balochistan.

AN
ACT
To regulate the transition of agricultural 
electricity consumers from subsidized electricity to 
solar energy, implement the Government of 
Pakistan (GoP) and Government of Balochistan 
(GoB) solarization agreements, and prevent 
subsidized agricultural consumers from 
reconnecting to the electricity distribution network 
and to prevent further electric theft and to provide 
for the matters connected therewith and ancillary 
thereto.

implementation of the solarization facility financed 
by the Government of Pakistan and the 
Government of Balochistan, to prevent subsidized 
agriculture consumers from reconnecting to the 
electricity distribution network in violation of the 
terms, and to criminalize unauthorized 
reconnections and electricity theft.
Short Title, 
Extent, and 
Commencement.

Balochistan Agricultural Solarization and 
Electricity Theft Prevention Act, 2025.

Balochistan and applies to all those beneficiaries 
of the solarization facility for agriculture tube wells 
who received the payments. 
(3) It shall come into force on such date 
as may be notified by the Provincial Government 
in the official Gazette.

EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
The Government of Balochistan recognizes Corporate Social
Responsibility (CSR) as a key mechanism for promoting inclusive
growth, social welfare, and environmental sustainability. The CSR
Guidelines 2025 have been formulated to establish a transparent,
accountable, and participatory framework for the planning,
approval, execution, and oversight of CSR initiatives across the
province.
These Guidelines aim to align CSR contributions from public and
private sector organizations, companies, development partners, and
non-governmental organizations with the provincial development
priorities. They provide a structured approach to ensure that CSR
resources are utilized effectively in sectors such as education, healthcare, women's empowerment,
youth skill development, drinking water and sanitation, agriculture, environmental protection,
sports, and community infrastructure.
The Guidelines outline clear mechanisms for project identification through community engagement
platforms such as Khuli Katcheri and public gatherings, ensuring that proposed schemes are need-
based, non-duplicative, and technically sound. Approval processes have been institutionalized
through District-level CSR Committees chaired by elected representatives and Deputy
Commissioners, while projects exceeding the financial threshold are routed through the Planning and
Development Department for higher-level lapproval.
To ensure transparency and accountability, all CSR transactions are to be carried out through formal
banking channels. with no cash withdrawals permitted. A robust monitoring and reporting
framework has been established, involving both district and provincial oversight mechanisms. The
Mines & Minerals Development and Energy Departments will serve as coordinating bodies for
reconciliation and reporting ofCSR funds, while a Provincial Oversight Conclave chaired by the
ChicfMinister will periodically review implementation progress and policy outcomes.
Fiscal discipline remains central to the CSR framework. The Auditor General ofPakistan,
external auditors, and the Internal Audit Unit of the Finance Department shall periodically
review CSR accounts to ensure compliance with financial regulations and prudent utilization
ofresources.
These Guidelines reaffirm the Government's commitment to strengthening collaboration
between the corporate sector, local communities, and government institutions for the
collective advancement of Balochistan. Through coordinated effort, transparency, and
shared responsibility. CSR can become a driving force for sustainable and inclusive
development in the province.
IMRAN ZARKOON
Secretary, Finance Department
(Government of Balochistan)

1. INTRODUCTION
Corporate Social Responsibility is a management concept whereby companies. government
agencies. public & private sector organizations, NGOS and international bodies integrate social and
environmental concerns in their business operations and interactions with their stakeholders. To
promote responsible business conduct that supports community growth for the public interest, the
elimination of the adverse practices impacting the public sphere and ensuring corporate
accountability. the Government ofBalochistan is pleased to issue the Guidelines on Corporate Social
Responsibility (CSR).
2. SCOPE AND APPLICABILITY
(i) These Guidelines are applicable on companies, goverment agencies, public & private sector
organizations, NGOS, international bodies and other entities that intend to undertake CSR
activities in Balochistans.jurisdiction.
(ii) These Guidelines are applicable on CSR activities in all sectors including: education, health,
environment. social development, community investment, governance and safety ete.
(iii) These Guidelines are applicable on the CSR activities undertaken as a result of legal and
regulatory requirements, commitment on voluntary basis beyond legal requirements.
(iv) These guidelines apply to planning, implementation. and reporting ofCSR activities, ensuring
transparency and accountability in all operations.
3. OBJECTIVES OF CSR GUIDELINES
(i) Conduct CSR activities, programs or projects with transparencyandaccountability;
(ii) Promote inclusive growth and development by addressing socio-economic
disparities;
(iii) Enhance environmental sustainability and mitigate the impact ofthe climate change;
(iv) Empower marginalized and vulnerable communities through targeted interventions:
(v) Foster ethical governance, transparency andaccountability in all operations; and
(vi) Encourage collaboration and partnerships with stakeholders for utilization of CSR
resources to maximizeimpact on the following:

(a) Children's Wellbeing and Education;
(b) Women's Empowerment;
(c) Healthcare;
(d) Drinking Water and Sanitation;
(e) Agriculture and Animal Husbandry:
(f) Skills Development ofYouth:
(g) Environmental Protection and Restoration;
(h) Sports and Cultural Activities;
(I) Development of Community Infrastructure.
4. PROJECT/SCHEME IDENTIFIFICATION FOR CSRACTIVITIES
(I) Project/Scheme for CSR activities shall be identified during public gatherings, Khuli
Katcheri or such like events where people gather in large number for interacting with the
elected leadership or Divisional/DistrictAdministration. The scheme identified shall havethe
following criteria
(a) Theproject-Scheme is suggestedby majority ofthe public;
(b) The scheme is not reflected in the provincial or federal PSDP or another CSR activity
such that there is not duplication ofthe scheme;
(c) Individual nature scheme shall not be eligible for CSR activities: and
(d) PC-1 shall be prepared and technically vetted for every scheme by the Engincers of
Local Government Department.
5. APPROVAL OF CSR PROJECT/SCHEME
(i) A project/scheme identified for CSR shall be approved by CSR Committee. The CSR
Committeeshallconsist ofthe following:
(a) Member Provincial Assembly of the concerned district/constituency where CSR
activity is to be executed.
(b) Deputy Commissioner ofthe concerned district.
(c) District Council Chairman.
(d) Additional Deputy Commissioner (General).
(e) Concerned Department Head.
(I) Representative ofthe concerned company/organization.

(ii) Member of the Provincial Assembly and the Deputy Commissioner shall Co-chair the
meeting ofCSR committee.

(iii) The Additional Deputy Commissioner (General) shall be the Secretary of the CSR
Committee. At least, three (3) members of the Committee excluding the Committee
Secretary shall form the quorum.

(iv) In case there are more than one Member of Provincial Assembly, then the Member of
Provincial Assembly in whose constituency the organization/company operates that
resulted into CSR. In case where the organization. company operates in more than one
constituency, The Chief Minister shall have the power to nominate the Co-Chair.

(v) The Committee observe the following while approving a Project/scheme:
(a) PC-I oftheproject/schemeisavailable.
(b) GPSCoordinates oftheprojectischeme chavel been taken.
(c) The project/scheme being approved has been shared with Planning &
Development Department and concerned administrative department for record
keeping gandi to avoid duplication.
(d) Ensuring to approve as maximum project/scheme as toavailability offunds.
(e) Strictly monitor that excess projects/schemes are not approved.
(I) Noproject/scheme shall be proposed against future cash flows.
(g) Multi-year planning should be generally be avoided. In case there is dire need
then the representative oft the organization. company who has contributed CSR
shall certify that the district will get funds in the next year.
(h) Noproject/scheme with recurrent expenditures shall bea approved.
(I) No projectischeme shall be approved that involve recruitment. If provision of
Human Resource is from another source, then such project/scheme could be
considered le.g. construction ofa building for shelter less school where positions
arealready created.
(vi) The Committee has the power to approve individual (single) projects/schemes worth Rs. 50

Development Department for approval through the DDWP/DSC or PDWP, as the case may
be.

(vii) There shall be no splitting of projects schemes for bringing the size ofthe project/scheme to
the mentioned threshold.

(viii) 50% of the CSR funds shall be spent in the sub-division where organization/company
operates that resulted into CSR.

(ix) The Members of the CSR Committee shall not be entitled for any payment from the CSR
funds; neither shall the account signatories be entitled to draw funds for any activity other
than CSR activities approved by the relevant forum.

(x) The funds allocated under CSR shall purely be utilized for public. social development and
shall not be utilized in goverment business or organization's own well-being. The CSR
activities that benefit only the employees ofthe organization/ agency or company and their
families shall not be considered as CSR activities.

(xi) All transactions shall be carried out through crossed cheques or other clectronic form and no
withdrawal from CSR funds shall be made in cash form.
6. PROCUREMENT OF CSR PROJECT/SCHEME
(i) Schemes approved at the district level shall be executed through village committees. Such
Committees shall be formed during the public interaction sessions mentioned in section 04.

(ii) There must be at least thirty-five (35) individuals in whose presence a committee offive (5)
individual is selected. Pictorial evidence ofthe gathering shall be taken.

(iii) The local councilor shall be added as the sixth member in case the community does not object
toit.

(iv) This committee shall select a contractor from the nearest villages and entrust him the work.

(v) Apayment register shall be maintained which shall be available for scrutiny and audit.

contractor.

(viii) Pictorial evidence ofthe project shall be taken at least at 5 stages ofthe project and be kept for
record for at least two years.

(ix) The Deputy Commissioner office shall also keep a record ofthe all schemes.
7. EXECUTION OF CSR FUNDED PROJECTS/SCHEMES
(i) The entire community, the CSR committec, related department and Deputy Commissioner
including the Assistant Commissioners, the Additional Deputy Commissioners, the
Tebsildars can inspect the schemes at various level lofexecution.

(ii) Payment to contractors shall be made in four (4) tranches of25%each.

(iii) Mobilization advance shall not be allowed.

(iv) Any complaint against the contractor for quality, shape and specification etc. shall be
addressed by the Village Committee. Ifthe grievance still exists. the Assistant Commissioner
of the sub-division shall resolve the issue by consulting the community members. The
Deputy Commissioner Office shall be the last stage for resolution ofcomplaint.
8. PROVINCIAL LEVEL COORDINATION FOR CSR ACTIVITIES
Mines &b Mineral Development and Energy Department shall be the two coordinating offices. Both
the departments shall reconcile the CSR funds from Exploration and Production companies as well as
other sources on quarterly basis. All other transfers such as voluntary CSR or grants etc. shall also be
recorded. Both the departments shall issue a report on quarterly basis and such report must be
circulated widely. The report shall also be placed on the various government website.

(I) Any other emerging business.
10. FISCALMANAGEMENT
The. Auditor General ofPakistan or External Auditors appointed under the Companies Act 2017. or
any other law for the time being in force, shall conduct annual audit oft the accounts maintained by
the concerned Deputy Commissioner to ensure utilization of CSR funds in a transparent manner.
The Internal Audit Unit ofFinance Department may be entitled to carry out audit ofthe accounts of
CSR based on direction ofthe Government.
11. REVIEW AND ADAPTATION

effectiveness in addressing the evolving aspects and impacts ofsocio-economic and environmental

MESSAGE FROM CHIEF MINISTER OF BALOCHISTAN
The Government of Balochistan is committed to providing equal opportunities for
women, girls and men in all spheres of public domain. We are determined to bring
reforms to make our policies and our work more gender-inclusive and ensure that
women’s empowerment not just a destination but a journey that our government
has decided to take on. We are making efforts to make the system more efficient,
gender-responsive and just, one that supports and encourages our women and
girls to play an active role in achieving the development goals including the SDGs.
Therefore, nothing is more important for us than strengthening, consolidating and promoting gender￾responsive policies and goals and we are determined to deepen and accelerate progress on key reforms
aimed at improving the lives of women and girls in Balochistan.
It is my honor to endorse the ‘Gender Equality and Women’s Empowerment Policy of the Government
of Balochistan’ which reflects strategic priority of our Government to introduce inclusive, sustainable and
meaningful reforms for creating an enabling environment for the women and girls of Balochistan. This is
indeed the first policy that has been aligned with the Sustainable Development agenda and reflects our
endeavors towards a just society where we see women’s participation in every sphere as an essential
prerequisite.
It is equally critical that all public institutions including law enforcement agencies support the
implementation of this policy in its true spirit. I see this policy as an opportunity and guiding document to
strengthen the women institutions including the Women Parliamentary Caucus, Ombudsperson for 
Protection Against Harassment at Workplace and the Balochistan Commission on the Status of Women
supported by the Women Development Department. I look forward to a visible change in the way we work
with greater participation of women in the economic sphere and ensure women’s easy access to justice so
that we could see a decrease in incidents of violence against women in the province. I am positive that all
stakeholders will support us in making optimal utilization of this policy, using innovative approaches, skills
and tools in order to promote Gender Equality and Women’s Empowerment in the province.
I am grateful to the Women Development Department who took the lead in steering this process and
putting together a well-structured and coherent analysis and a measurable plan for pro-women
institutional reforms in public and private sectors in Balochistan. I would also like to extend my gratitude
to UN Women for their invaluable support in our collective mission to mainstream gender in our work and
to create development pathways based on gender equality in Balochistan.
I declare complete and comprehensive support for the timely and smooth implementation of this policy
which would be institutionalized and regularly reviewed in order to demonstrate concrete results for the
women and girls of the province.
Mir Jam Kamal Khan Alyani
Chief Minister, Balochistan

The initial Gender Equality and Women’s Empowerment Policy was notified in 2013, under a caretaker

The main purpose of this policy is to remove structural barriers, reform restrictive gender norms and
streamline disparities through horizontal and vertical management and coordination. It provides a
framework for ensuring women’s full and effective participation in all spheres of life, providing equal
opportunities for leadership at all levels of decision-making in political, economic and public life, and 
enhancing accountability and institutional frameworks. The aim is to develop and put forward a policy
that is clearly aligned with SDGs and other commitments that the provincial government is duty bound to
fulfill regarding women’s rights. Thus, this document is presented in view of a fast-evolving context which
necessitated the formulation of an updated policy framework encompassing key policy, legislative and
institutional initiatives.
Led by the WDD, the current policy is envisioned to be coordinated by an overarching body, periodically
presided over by the top executive leadership of the province to ensure consistent policy direction and
meaningful stock-taking. Accompanied by an elaborate implementation framework and a workplan for
the next five years, this policy framework essentially centers on a set of priorities along with key
performance indicators.

inclusive approach as it not only drew upon considerable research literature but also incorporated diverse

enhancing accountability and institutional frameworks. The aim is to develop and put forward a policy
that is clearly aligned with SDGS and other commitments that the provincial government is duty bound to
fulfill regarding women's rights. Thus, this document is presented in view of a fast-evolving context which
necessitated the formulation of an updated policy framework encompassing key policy, legislative and
institutional initiatives.

Led by the WDD, the current policy is envisioned to be coordinated by an overarching body, periodically
presided over by the top executive leadership of the province to ensure consistent policy direction and
meaningful stock-taking. Accompanied by an elaborate implementation framework and a workplan for
the next five years, this policy framework essentially centers on a set of priorities along with key
performance indicators.

Last but not the least, it is important to highlight that the policy development process took a holistic and
inclusive approach as it not only drew upon considerable research literature but also incorporated diverse
views of stakeholders who were duly consulted during its formulation process. The WDD led the process
of the formulation of this document, which has been drafted and finalized in consultation with and after
obtaining recommendations from a wide range of stakeholders across Balochistan, as well as the review
of key official documents. It is the culmination of various levels of information and insight-gathering,
including a detailed review of government structures and mechanisms that would allow this government-
wide policy to work.

STRATEGIC PRIORITIZATION FRAMEWORK
1. Women’s Economic Empowerment
The Government of Balochistan is striving for inclusive economic growth and sustainable development.
The role, participation and contribution of women and girls in economic development processes is
recognized as crucial to long term success of economic policies, packages and programmes that the
Government is seeking to implement in the next few years. The Women Economic Empowerment (WEE)
Council has been notified by the WDD to safeguard the interests of women entrepreneurs at all levels and
facilitate their access to the market. Specific steps are required to ensure provision of equitable economic
opportunities in order to meet the objectives of gender-sensitive economic empowerment of all citizens
including women. Given the specific economic context and business outlook of the province, this policy
emphasizes pro-women interventions in areas which can yield maximum economic benefits to
Balochistan’s women and girls. Key priority sectors include agriculture, livestock, handicrafts, technical
and vocational trainings and other small scale and home-based industries.
Vision 2025 is the key planning document of the Government of Pakistan that focuses on agricultural
productivity, urban development, health and education, enhancing safety nets and improving institutional
performance. It recognizes women’s role in the economy and their concentration in informal work.
Women in Balochistan are primarily employed in livestock and handicrafts work wherein they constantly
face market exploitation. Training and skill development as well as marketing and credit facilities for
women are minimal. In order to ensure sustainable development and economic growth there is a strong
need to emphasize on human centered development including reducing gender-based inequality in terms
of women’s access to employment and decent living. The Government is cognizant of the fact that
women's empowerment is pivotal for sustainable development.
Policy Objectives:
 To create employment and income generation opportunities for women and girls in the formal
economy and informal sector thereby supporting women and girls to earn a decent living wage and
benefit from gainful and productive employment, free from exploitation.
 To recognize and address women’s unpaid labor and contributions to the household and the national
economy.
 To undertake reforms to give women equal rights to economic resources, as well as access to
ownership and control over land and other forms of property, financial services, inheritance and
natural resources.

Policy Priorities:

empowerment policy, including consideration for ILO Conventions, specifically Conventions 100
(Equal Remuneration Convention, 1951); 111 (Discrimination -Employment and Occupation￾Convention, 1958); 189 (Domestic Workers Convention, 2011); and 177 (Home Work Convention,

2. Social Empowerment
Women empowerment and low literacy levels among girls is a problem acrossthe province. Due to strong
tribal customs, religious influences and male dominance, women have limited or no role in decision
making at all levels. High maternal mortality rates, malnutrition, early marriages and scarcity of basic
services with restricted mobility puts women in a subservient role. This is manifested in the way the
women are given roles in the political arena and in the public sector representation. In Balochistan, there
is less than 2% representation of women in the bureaucracy, no women in provincial cabinet, most of the
political decision making, budget making processes, and planning lacks the gender perspective. Any effort
to integrate gender in the social context remains a challenge.
2.1 Education
Education is a right denied to many children across Pakistan, but the state of literacy, particularly of
females is dismal in Balochistan. The statistics paint a bleak picture, with less than 2% of rural women
educated and only 26 % overall female literacy in the province. As many as 70% girls drop out of school as
cited by sources in the Education Department. And Balochistan is at bottom with the lowest literacy rate
of 44%.34 Recently the Government announced co-education across the province at primary level which
may help increase girls’ enrolment as this will provide increased access to nearby schools vicinities which
was also one of the major factors contributing to girls drop out.
Along with these initiatives, the Government aims to enhance awareness in society about the importance
of female education by enhancing gender sensitivity through education. For this purpose, WDD envisions
developing gender sensitive textbooks and curriculum with the help of Education Department.

2.2 Women’s Health
Balochistan is characterized by disproportionate distribution of health services among various districts
and across the urban/ rural divide within the province, where the major health facilities are in the
provincial capital. The latest estimate reveals an alarmingly high maternal mortality rate for the province.
This GEWE policy aims to secure universal health coverage for the women and girls of Balochistan. The
overall intent is to make sure all girls and women, particularly mothers and newborn babies are provided
with timely healthcare facilities, services and opportunities without consideration of socio-economic
background. This policy will complement the health policy of the province which seeks to incorporate
gender-sensitive approaches for a preventive, promotive and curative healthcare regime for all. Policy
priorities will be targeted towards ensuring women and girls’ access to primary, secondary and tertiary
healthcare facilities.
Cultural norms promoting sexual ignorance and purity of women block their access to information about
preventive measures. Gendered power imbalances make it difficult for women to negotiate safer sexual
practices with their partners, and economic dependence and fear of violence can effectively force them
to consent to unprotected sex. Lack of awareness regarding menstrual hygiene is also a major cause of
infectious disease among young girls and women. Women receive inadequate care and treatment both
because it is directly withheld from them and because what is being provided is inaccessible and unsuited
to their health needs. The burden of caring for their dependents and themselves can become
overwhelming, sinking families into poverty and destitution, because women lack access to economic
resources and are the hardest hit by the lack of social support.
Policy Objectives:
 Provincial Government to formulate a progressive, forward-looking Health and Population Policy, and
ensure gender mainstreaming in people with disability and people with age proposed bills.
 Strengthening Basic Health Units (BHUs) to expand community-based Lady Health Workers (LHW)
program
 Increased awareness about reproductive health for behavioral change and advocacy for enhancing
budget within health sector on maternal health.

Women are not only the hardest hit by this pandemic, they are also the backbone of recovery in 
communities. Putting women and girls at the center of all the response by the government will 
fundamentally drive better and more sustainable development outcomes for all, support a more 
rapid recovery, and place the world back on a footing to achieve the Sustainable Development 
Goals.
This policy proposes that every COVID-19 response plans, and every recovery package and 
budgeting of resources, needs to address the gender impacts of this pandemic. This means: (1) 
including women and women’s organizations in COVID-19 response planning and decision-making; 
(2) transforming the inequities of unpaid care work into a new, inclusive care economy that works 
for everyone; and 
(3) designing socio-economic plans with an intentional focus on the lives and futures of women 
and girls.

1. Gender-based violence, including domestic violence, is mitigated and reduced
2. Social protection and economic stimulus packages serve women and girls
3. People support and practise equal sharing of care work
4. Women and girls lead and participate in COVID-19 response planning and decision-making
5. Data and coordination mechanisms include gender perspectives

4. Women’s Access to Justice
In Balochistan, violence against women and girls is rooted in patriarchal norms and class or ethnicity￾based oppression. Women are prevented from enjoying existing rights because of the prevalence of
negative customary practices and attitudes.
The focus on the reproductive role of women along with strong emphasis on female chastity are the
underlying causes of early marriage, high fertility rates and psychological and mental abuse of women.
Violence beginsin the form of discrimination against a girl child and continuesin variousformsthroughout
the life of a woman. Multiple reasons include ignorance about rights and responsibilities, minimal access
to judicial and redressal mechanisms, expensive and prolonged processes for accessing justice, poor
implementation of the law, and weak state support services for victims of violence. Moreover, affirmative
provisions of the Constitution are seldom implemented to establish real and substantial equality.
Institutional mechanisms to support victims of violence have been set up but these are as yet insufficient
and need to be strengthened and utilized. There are only three women crises centers and shelter homes
in Balochistan, and only one Dar-ul-Aman. In addition to the low numbers, the existing facilities remain
unsatisfactory with the biggest issue of non-availability of medico-legal services.
In terms of domestic violence against women, the Human Rights Commission of Pakistan (2014) revealed
a 33% increase from 2008 to 2014 in violence against women. Balochistan passed its Balochistan Domestic
Violence (Protection & Prevention) Act 2014, however its implementation is still not at the desired
standard.
This policy recommends a holistic approach to ensure equitable access to justice for all women and girls
of Balochistan.
Policy Objective:
To improve women and girls’ access to integrated systems of justice, protection and rehabilitation/
reintegration, by informing them about laws and related processes and existing services, facilitating their
engagement with the justice system, undertaking necessary legislative and administrative actions, and
building effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels.

viewed as incidental instead of being an essential part of such policies in Pakistan. This is substantiated by
the lack of policies, frameworks and plans that include an analysis of gender-related challenges and
consequences among climate change measures, strategies and actions.

Collecting province-wide data on key priority areas shall remain a core responsibility of the WDD
regardless of the extent of cooperation of the respective departments. For this purpose, the WDD's M&E
plan along with workplan of this policy spell out a number of public opinion surveys, impact assessments
and research studies in order to generate credible official data for the purpose of informed decision-
making for the implementation of the gender equality and women's empowerment policy.

To sum up, a well-functioning M&E system operated by gender M&E experts of the WDD is key for
successful adherence to policy goals and priorities. To achieve this, WDD is strategically positioned to play
al leadership role.

NOTIFICATION
[24August, 1970]
No. H-Pol-15(37)70.- - In exercise of the powers conferred by Section 11 of the West Pakistan
Publication of the Book (Regulation and Control) Ordinance, 1969 (West Pakistan Ordinance
No. XV of 1969) read with Article 19 of West Pakistan Dissolution Order, 1970 and in
supersession, of the West Pakistan Publication of Books (Regulation and Control) Rules 1969,
the Governor of Balochistan is pleased to make the following rules namely:
1. Short title and commencement. (1) These rules may be called the
Balochistan Publication of Books (Regulation and Control) Rules, 1970.
(2) They shall come into force at once.

These rules have been made by the Government of Balochistan, Home Department, vide its notification No. H-Pol-15(37)/70,
dated 24th August, 1970; and published in the Balochistan Gazette, dated 24August, 1970.
Spelling of the word "Baluchistan", wherever it appears in these rules, is corrected by insertion of letter "o" instead of E"u"; as per
Government of Balochistan, S&GAD's Notification No. SORI (4) 6/ S&GAD-89, dated 18th. June, 1989.

2. Definitions. ― In these rules, unless there is anything repugnant in the subject or
context, ―
(a) “Director” means the Director of Information, Government of Balochistan,
Quetta.
(b) “Forms” means a form appended to these rules.
(c) “Ordinance” means the West Pakistan Publication of Book (Regulation and
Control) Ordinance, 19691
.
(d) “Section” means a section of the Ordinance.
3. Application for permission. ―(1) An application under subsection (1) of section 4
for permission to print or publish a book or work shall be submitted in Form A’ to the Director ‛
and shall be accompanied by a copy of the original book or work in respect of which permission
is sought.
(2) The contents of the application shall be verified on solemn affirmation by the
applicant to be true.
4. Disposal of application. ― (1) On receipt of an application under rules
3, the Director , after making such inquiry as he deems fit, may, for reasons to be recorded in
writing either grant the permission applied for or if in his opinion the book or work in respect of
which the application is made, is prejudicial to the national interest or culture, refuse permission:
Provided that the Director shall not refuse such permission without giving
applicant an opportunity for of being heard and showing cause against the proposed refusal. 
(2) Where permission to print or publish a book or work is granted the applicant
shall be furnished by the authority granting the permission, a certificate on Form “B’’.
(3) Where permission to print a book or a work is refused by the Director, he shall
furnish the applicant a copy of the grounds for such refusal.
5. Appeal or review. ― A petition for appeal or review under subsection (1) of section 5
shall be accompanied by a copy of the order of the Director refusing permission.
6. Maintenance of registers. ― (1) The Director shall maintain a register in Form
‘C’ of books and work permission for the printing or publishing whereof has been granted under
the Ordinance.
(2) The Director shall maintain a separate register in Form ‘D’ of books and works
permission for the printing or publishing where of under the Ordinance has been refused.

GOVERNMENT OF BALOCHISTAN
LOCAL GOVERNMENT RURAL DEVELOPMENT
AND AGROVILLES DEPARTMENT
(Balochistan Local Government Board)
NOTIFICATION
Dated Quetta, the 23rd May, 2023
No. 1-78/2023 (BLGB) A.0-IV/4559-751. In exercise of the power conferred
by Section 141 of the Balochistan Local Government Act, 2010 (V of 2010) the
Government of Balochistan is pleased to make the Balochistan Local Councils
(Budget) Rules, 2023 and to promulgate the following Rules:-

Printed by the Chief Controller, Government Printing and Stationery Department, Balochistan Quetta.
Price Rs. 560/- D.No.190-230-Copies-11-2023.

2

1. Short title, commencement and application: (1) These rules may be called
the Balochistan Local Councils (Budget) Rules, 2022.
(2) They shall come into force at once.
(3) They shall apply to all the local councils in Balochistan.
2. Definitions: (1) In these rules, unless there is anything repugnant in the
subject or context:
(a) "Act" means the Balochistan Local Government Act, 2010 (Act No.
V of 2010) and subsequent amendments including but not limited to
The Balochistan Local Government (Amendment) Act, 2022 Act No.
XXIli of 2022
(b) "Actuals" means the actual figures of receipts or expenditure
relating to a financial year, duly reconciled with Finance Department;
(c) "Annual Budget Statement" means a statement showing of the
estimated receipts, distinguished between revenue receipts and
capital receipts, in the local fund, of the local council and the
estimated expenditure therefrom, for a financial period covered under
the budget, required to be laid before the Council before the
commencement of that year;
(d) "Annual Development Plan" means the Annual Development Plan
: submitted along with the Annual Budget Statement, which includes
the details of capital and revenue expenditure proposed for the
various developmental projects in the budget for a financial year;
(e) "Appropriation" means the amount provided in the budget
estimates against a detailed object or part of amount. placed at the
disposal of the disbursing officer to meet expenditure for a specific
purpose or on a specific item;
(f) "Authority" means an Authority empowered under section-100 of
the Act for sanctioning of the budget of a local councit;
(g) "Board" means as inserted under (li-a) through Balcchistan Local
Government (Amendment) Act, 2022 Act No. XXIII of 2022
(h) "Budget" means a statement of estimated receipts and expenditure
of the local council for a financial period;

3

(i) "Budget Calendar" means a list and timeline of budget activities to
be carried out during a financial year for the preparation ofthe budget
for the ensuing financial year given in Second Schedule;
() "Budget Period or Financial Period" means the period of one year
from 1st July to 30th June (both days Inclusive) or an interim period
other than a complete one year, as decided by the Government in a
particular case;
(k) "Budget scrutiny committee of the division" means the
committee created to review the Local Council budget as prescribed
under the amendment of Section 70 under The Balochistan Local
Government (Amendment) Act, 2022 Act no. XXIII of 2022. The
committee shall consist of Divisional Director Local Councils,
Secretary of the Local Council concerned, Deputy Director (Admin)
Local Councils, Director (Tech) Local Councils, an Assistant Director
(B&A) and any co-opted member. Provided that the Chairman of the
Budget Committee shall be the Divisional Director Local Council and
Deputy Director (Admin) shall be its ex-officio Secretary.
(I) "Capital expenditure" within the meaning of assets, means the
expenditure on assets with useful life of more than one year and,
within the meaning of liabilities, means expenditure on repayment of
loans and advances, and includes;
(i) acquisition, enhancement or improvement of physical assets;
(ii) investments and deposits;
(iii) execution of works including construction of building, roads,
structures etc.; and
(iv) principal repayment of loans and advances.
(m) "Capital Receipts" mean the receipts from sources other than
revenue and include;
(i) proceeds from disposal of capital assets;
(ii) sale of investments;
(ii) loans; and
(iv) advances and deposits.
(n) "Charged expenditure" or "Expenditure Charged upon the Local
Fund" means the expenditure specified in section 98 of the Act and
is not subject to vote of the local council;

4

(0) "Collecting Office" means the Office responsible for estimation and
realization of the receipts and income of the Local Councii and
includes all Heads of Offices designated as such by the Principal
Accounting Officer. For the purposes of these Rules, wherever the
word "Collecting Office" is used, it may be read as Collecting
WingSecton/@ranch/Oficar.
(p) "Current Expenditure" means the expenditure other than the
development expenditure;
(q) "Demand for Grant" means the proposal made to the Council on
the recommendation of the Mayor or Chairman for allocation of a
certain sum out of the local fund, in a financial year; and on its

CHAPTER-V

21. Preparation of estimates of the current expenditure: (1) The estimates of

(2) The current budget estimates shall be prepared in Forms BR-3 to BR-5
22. Instructions for preparation of estimates of the current expenditure:
The following principles shail be observed while preparing the estimates of the
current Expenditure:
(a) the estimates of expenditure shall be prepared diligently and
accurately keeping in view the key performance indicators;
(b) while preparing the revised estimates, the drawing and disbursing
officer shall take into consideration the actual expenditure available
for the latest period of the financial year and include actual figures of
the corresponding period of the previous financial year;
(c) all material reasons, facts and circumstances relied upon in adopting
figures for the revised estimates for the current financial year and
annual budget estimates for the next financial year shall be recorded
clearly;
(d) provision for any foreseeable expenditure shall be included therein;
(e) each provision is restricted to the absolute minimum necessary sum;
(f) the estimates for each financial year shall provide only such
expenditure as are to be actually incurred during the next financial
year;
(g) where the local Council or the Government specifies minimum ratio
for development and non-development expenditure or for any other
object of expenditure, the prescribed constraint shall be observed in
the estimates of the current expenditure;
(h) the rise in current expenditure shall be proportionate to the rise in
revenue receipts and no deficit or debt shall be included in the
estimates;
(i) adequate provisions shall be made for all items of the charged
expenditure;

(m) the allowances of the employees shall be calculated as per their

(n) The revised budget of the ongoing financial year shall be based on

expenditure during the first eight months of the current,financial year and last
four months of the corresponding financial year may be considered as a guide
to ascertain ratio of budget-actual trend.

23. Balance, deficit budget. - (1). The surplus potential of the council for a year
shall be the excess of revenue income over revenue expenditure, and where there
is no surplus potential, the budget will be in deficit.
(2) The budget of a council shall, as far as possible, be balanced and the
revenue and development expenditure shall not exceed the revenue and
capital receipts of the council, but where a deficit budget is unavoidable, the
fact shall be brought to the notice of the Government by the 1st day of May
each year,
(3) Where the Revenue Budget of a council cannot be balanced, Government
may direct a special study of the finances of the council and, as a
consequence of such study, require the council to take such action for the
improvement of its finances as may be specified.

CHAPTER-X

RE-APPROPRIATIONS AND SUPPLEMENTARY GRANTS
54. Expenditure not provided in the Schedule of Authorized Expenditure: In
case of unavoidable and unforeseen circumstances which require incurring the
expenditure in excess of the allocations or some expenditure which is not
mentioned in the schedule of authorized expenditure, necessary funds for such
expenditure may be provided through re-appropriation or supplementary grant or
both as in the manner prescribed.
55. Re-appropriation: The local council functionaries shall re-appropriate in
accordance with the re-appropriation powers delegated to them by the Council in
the manner prescribed.
(2) Procedure for Re-Appropriation: (1) the concerned drawing and
disoursing officer may prepare a proposal for re-appropriation and process it
through the head of offices. No re-appropriation shall be made from grant to
the other.

(3) In case the re-appropriation is beyond the limit set by the Council, it shall
require approval of the Council and, for the purpose, the head of offices shall
prepare a proposal for re-appropriation of funds and forward it, through the head
of accounts branch, to the Chief Officer, Mayor or Chairman for approval of the
Council as in the manner prescribed.
56. Supplementary Grant: (1) In case a head of office considers that the need
for additional funds for which funds cannot be provided through re-appropriation
has arisen, he shall make a proposal for supplementary grant to the head of
accounts branch.
(2) The proposal shall be accompanied by an explanatory note justifying the
supplementary grant and the source of funding for the purpose.
57. Supplementary Budget Statement: (1) The supplementary grants approved
during the financial year shall be consolidated by the head of accounts branch in
the form of a supplementary budget statement with his recommendations
particularly with regard to the availability of funds.
(2) The form and manner in which the supplementary budget statement is
presented to the local council shall be the same as prescribed for the annual
budget statement.
58. Distribution and communication of Supplementary Grants: On approval
of supplementary budget statement by the Council, a schedule supplementary
statement of expenditure shall be submitted to. the Mayor or Chairman for
authentication and the head of respective Local Council Accounts Office shall
distribute the supplementary grants to the respective Head of office and
communicate the break-up of the grants to the drawing and disbursing officers and
the respective Local Council Accounts Office/Officer,

immediately in the local fund and entered in the proper receipt head.

Officers and take corrective measures.
(3) The revised targets of receipts/ if any, shall be communicated by the head
of accounts office to the collecting officers and heads of offices.

(b) consolidate and prepare budget documents for approval; and

THE BALOCHISTAN PROHIBITION OF SHEESHA SMOKING
ACT, 2016

(Balochistan Act V of 2016)

[29th September, 2016]

An Act to provide for the prohibition of sheesha
smoking in Balochistan.

Preamble. WHEREAS, it is expedient in the public interest to
provide for the prevention of sheesha smoking in the
Balochistan in order to save human life and to provide for
matters connected therewith and incidental there to;

It is hereby enacted as follows: —

Short title and 1. (1) This Act may be called the Balochistan
commencemen- Prohibition of Sheesha Smoking Act, 2016.
t. (2) It extends to the whole of the Balochistan,
except the Tribal Areas.

(3) It shall come into force at once.

Definitions. 2. In this Act, unless the subject or context otherwise
requires, the following expressions shall have the meanings
hereby respectively assigned to them —

(a) “Chemical drug” means any controlled
drug
declared under any law as such and used in
sheesha smoking;

(b) “Flavor/tobacco” means a mixture of the chemical
different (kasbo) or any other injurious and
dangerous material, mixed in tobacco for the
purpose of sheesha smoking;

(c) “Government” means the Government of
Balochistan;

(d) “Place” means a street, road, ports, garden, play
ground, graveyard, hotel restaurant, motel, mess,
club, house, building, tent, vessel, any restaurant
or hotel roof and open space; and

1 This Act was passed by the Balochistan Assembly on 21st September, 2016; assented to by the Governor of Balochistan on 29th
September, 2016; and published in the Balochistan Gazette (Extraordinary) No. 115, dated 29th September, 2016.

(e) "Sheesha smoking" means the act of sheesha
smoking at any place with tobacco, different
flavours, carbon for fire.

Prohibition of
Sheesha
smoking. 3. No person, individually or collectively, shall
manufacture, sell, purchase, store, keep use or import or in any
manner engage himself in sheesha smoking

Offence. 4. Any offence committed under this Act shall be a
cognizable and bailable offence.

Summary trial of
offence. 5. Notwithstanding anything contained in any other law for
the time being in force, the act of sheesha smoking shall be
tried summarily under chapter XXII of the Code of Criminal
Procedure 1989 (V of 1989).

Punishment. 6. Whoever —
(a) commits or abets to commit an act of sheesha
smoking; shall be punished with imprisonment
for a term which may extend to six months or
with fine which may extend to five thousand
rupees or both;
(b) manufacturers, sells or offers for sale sheesha
like (glass hookah); or
(c) manufacturers, stores, sells, keeps or offers for
sale material like different flavors, sheesha (glass
hookah); or
(d) imports sheesha (glass hookah) and other related
material like different flavors etc shall be
punished with imprisonment for a term which
may extend to three years or with fine which
may extend to one Hundred thousand rupees or
with both.

Overriding effect. 7. The provisions of this Act shall be in addition to and not
in derogation of any other law for the time being in force.

Power to make
rules. 8. The Government may by notification in the official
gazette, make rules for carrying out the purposes of this Act.

35. (i) The Cess Inspector shall inspect every cess post in his circle at least once a day.

(ii) On the occasion of an inspection, the Cess Inspector shall among other matters, check all registers maintained at the cess post and all cess receipts.

36. The Extra Assistant Director of Agriculture, (Economic & Marketing) shall inspect every cess post at least once a week.

37. The Deputy Director of Agriculture (E&M) shall inspect every cess post at least once a month.

38. The Director of Agriculture Balochistan, shall inspect every cess post at least once in three months.

39. The officers authorised to inspect the working of the cess collection scheme and the officers of Audit Department in the name of cess collection scheme may inspect any cess post.

40. An Inspection Register shall be kept at every cess post and the result of every inspection shall be recorded in such register.

41. The Cess Inspector, Extra Assistant Director, shall verify that adequate action has been taken on the various observations and recommendations in the inspection notes and shall record the action taken in the appropriate Inspection Register.

42. If as a result of inspection, irregularities are noticed in the working of the cess post shall be reported to Extra Assistant Director of Agriculture (E&M) who will investigate the cess.

43. If as a result of an inspection, it is found that some amount of cess on any goods has been undercharged the matter shall be investigated by the inspecting officer.

44. If as a result of any investigation, it is proved that some cess has been undercharged in any case the cess shall be recovered from the concerned person and he shall be required by a notice to pay the amount within the period specified in the notice, stop shall be taken to recover it as an arrear of land revenue.

45. If in the case of any cess assessment, the export is not traceable, or the amount cannot be recovered from the amount shall be recovered from the cess collection concerned if the enquiry is found to be at fault.

CHAPTER IV.

46. Any Inspecting Officer who finds a person in possession of goods which he has reasons to believe to have been exported, or to have been exported by any person without the payment of cess receipt, may demand the cess receipt from such person and if the person refuses to furnish such information as may be asked and permit the officer demanding it to inspect the goods.

47. If the person in charge of the goods held, up for check has no receipt or if the inspecting officer finds reasons to believe that the full amount of the cess has not been paid on the goods or that the goods cannot tally with the amount entered in his receipt, the Inspecting Officer shall investigate the cess.

48. If as a result of any investigation, under the rules, the Inspecting Officer satisfied that the person in charge of goods is guilty of the evasion of cess, he shall register a case of the evasion of cess against him.

49. If the Inspection Officer has reasons to believe that some goods are being exported or smuggled without the payment of cess, he may organise a raid and intercept such goods during the course of transit.

50. In the organisation of any raid under rules, the Inspecting Officer may obtain assistance from the police as may be necessary.

51. For the purpose of any check under these rules the Inspecting Officer may be signal required that the driver of any vehicle to halt and such driver shall halt the vehicle and permit the Inspecting officer to inspect the Vehicle and the goods carried therein.

6

CHAPTER X.

INVESTIGATIONS.

52. The Director of Agriculture or Deputy Director of Agriculture (F&M) may "Set Motion" on
the complaint or representation of any person order on investigation in any case governed by the provi-
sion of these rules.
53. Where a case is required to be investigated under any of the provision of these rules, an investigation
report shall be drawn up.
54. Where an investigation is likely to take some time, such inspection report shall be drawn up and
forwarded to the Cess Collection Department in the First instance and investigation report shall be
forwarded as soon as it is completed.
55. Every case of investigation shall be registered at Cess Collection Department in the investigation
register.
56. The Deputy Director of Agriculture (F&M) shall check the investigation register at least once
a month and take such steps as may be necessary to ensure that no case of investigation is held up, and
that adequate action is taken on every case investigated under these rules.
57. Where a case of the evasion of Cess has been registered against a person such person may apply
for the composition of the offence, and if he pays the Cess and any amount by way of composition
equivalent to the Cess, the inspecting officer may compound the offence and issue a new
ordinary inspecting receipt/pass.
58. Where a case of an evasion of Cess is not compounded the person concerned shall be prosecuted.
All cases of evasion of Cess shall be registered in the investigation register.
59. Where any case of the evasion of Cess is required to be forwarded to Cess Collection Department,
the inspecting officer shall make arrangements as may be necessary for the securing of goods to the
Cess Collection Department.
60. If a person is not prepared to take the goods to Cess Collection Department, the inspecting officer
shall pass an order for seizure of goods.
61. The goods seized under note shall comprise three foil's the third foil shall be
handed over to the person from whom the goods have been seized and the Second foil shall be forwarded
to the Cess Collection Department.
62. A seizure Register shall be maintained at the Cess Collection Department in which all transaction
about the seizure of goods and the release or disposal of such goods shall be recorded.
63. If the person whose goods have been seized under these rules pay the cess and the case aga-
inst him is compounded the goods shall be released and entry to that effect shall be made in the seizure
Register.
64. If the goods seized are not claimed within the period specified in the order of seizure or if claimed,
but the cess is not paid, the goods may be sold or disposed of in such manner as may be determined by
the Deputy Director of Agriculture (F&M). If any balance is left after the adjustment of the claim
of cess collection Department, it shall be refunded to the person concerned, provided the person con-
cerned, if not traceable, shall be deposited in fund of Cess Collection seizure.

CHAPTER XI.

DIARIES, REPORTS AND REVIEWS.

65. The Extra Assistant Director of Agriculture (E&M) and the Cess Inspector shall submit a dia-
ry for every working day such diaries shall be reviewed by the Deputy Director of Agriculture at least once
a week.

7

66. The Deputy Director of Agriculture (F&M) shall at the close of each month submit a report to
the Director of Agriculture about the working of Cess Collection Department during the preceding
month.
67. At the close of each year the Director of Agriculture shall submit to the Controlling authority
a detailed report on the working of Cess Collection Department during the preceding year.
68. If due to any miscalculation or error any amount under these rules has been charged in excess
from any person such person may within thirty days of such payment apply to the Deputy Director of
Agriculture (F&M) for the refund of the amount charged in excess.
69. Every application made under rule 70 shall be investigated and if an investigation the claim is
founded to be correct the amount charged in excess shall be refunded to the person concerned.

THE PROHIBITION OF SHEESHA SMOKING IN BALOCHISTAN ACT 2016.
Act No. V of 2016
AN
ACT
to provide for the prohibition of sheesha Smoking in
