2

Preamble.
Whereas, it is expedient in the public interest to
provide for the prevention of sheesha smoking in the
Balochistan in order to save human life and to provide
for matters connected therewith and incidental there to;

It is hereby enacted as follow:-

Short title and
commencement.
1. (1) This Act may be called as the Balochistan
Prohibition of sheesha Smoking Act, 2016.
(2) It extends to the whole of the Balochistan,
except the Tribal Areas.
(3) It shall come into force at once.

Definitions.
2. In this Act, unless the subject or context
otherwise requires, the following expressions shall
have the meanings hereby respectively assigned to
them -
a) "Chemical drug" means any controlled drug
declared under any law as such and used in
sheesha smoking;
b) "Flavour/tobacco" means a mixture of the
chemical different (kasbo) or any other
injurious and dangerous material, mixed in
tobacco for the purpose of sheesha smoking;
c) "Government" means the Government of
Balochistan;
d) "Place" means a street, road, ports, garden,
play ground, graveyard, hotel restaurant,
motel, mess, club, house, building, tent,
vessel, any restaurant or hotel roof and open
space; and
e) "Sheesha smoking" means the act of
sheesha smoking at any place with tobacco,
different flavours, carbon for fire.

3

Prohibition of
Sheesha smoking. 3. No person, individually or collectively, shall
manufacture, sell, purchase, store, keep use or import
or in any manner engage himself in sheesha smoking.

Offence. 4. Any offence committed under this Act shall be a
cognizable and bailable offence.

Summa-y trial of
offence. 5. Notwithstanding anything contained in any other
law for the time being in force, the act of sheesha
smoking shall be tried summarily under chapter XXII of
the Code of Criminal Procedure 1898 (V of 1898).

Punishment. 6. Whoever -

a) commits or abets to commit an act of sheesha
smoking, shall be punished with imprisonment
for a term which may extend to six months or
with fine which may extend to five thousand
rupees or both;

b) manufacturers, sells or offers for sale sheesha
like (glass hookah); or

c) manufacturers, stores, sells, keeps or offers for
sale material like different flavours, sheesha
(glass hookah); or

d) imports sheesha (glass hookah) and other
related material like different flavours etc shall
be punished with imprisonment for a term which
may extend to three years or with fine which
may extend to one Hundred thousand rupees or
with both.

Overriding effect. 7. The provisions of this Act shall be in addition to
and not in derogation of any other law for the time
being in force.

3. ELIGIBILITY.

(1) A Government Servant, who is posted at Quetta and does not own
house either in his name or in the names of his spouse or dependent
children, shall be eligible for allotment of residential accommodation.
(2) (a) In case both he and his spouse are in Government Service only
one of them shall be eligible for allotment of residential
accommodation.
(b) A single Government Servant may be allotted accommodation
according to the entitlement only where there is no Government
Servant on the waiting list of that class.
(c) In case both he and his spouse are in Government Service and a
Government accommodation is allotted to either one of them, the
other spouse will no longer be eligible for House Requisition
Allowance.

4. CLASSIFICATION AND ENTITLEMENT.

(1) The limits of entitlement of Government Servants for allotment of
accommodation in Quetta shall be as under :-

| S.No. | Type of Accommodation | Entitlement. |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 1. | "A" Type Residences | Grade 20-22 and Additional Secretaries. |
| 2. | "B" Type Residences | Grade 19- Dy. Secretaries. |
| 3. | "C" Type Houses / Flats. | Grade 17-18 Officers. |
| 4. | "D" Type Quarters | Grade 16 Officers. |
| 5. | "E" Type Quarters | Grade 11-15 Officials |
| 6. | "F" Type Quarters | Grade 08-10 Officials |
| 7. | "G" Type Quarters | Grade 05-07 Officials |
| 8. | "H" Type Quarters | Grade 01-04 Officials. |

(2) A Government Servant shall be eligible to a residential
accommodation of his class, unless Government may from time to time
reserve for different categories of Government servant provided that
nothing contained in this rule shall debar a Government servant from
the allotment of an accommodation inferior than to the one to which he
is entitled if such Government Servant has no objection to allotment of
such inferior accommodation.

ALLOTMENT COMMITTEE.

(1) There shall be a House Allotment Committee constituted by the
Government, consisting of a Chairman and three members.
(2) The Government shall appoint a Civil Service Officer in the Services &
General Administration Department, who shall act as Secretary of the
Committee and perform such functions as determined by the
Committee.
(3) The Committee shall meet at least once a month.

5. ALLOTMENT.

(1) Subject to availability of accommodation, a Government Servant shall
be allotted a residential accommodation in accordance with the
provisions of these rules and in order of merit assigned to him under
rule 7.
(2) The allotment shall be made by the Estate Officer, under the order of
the Chairman House Allotment Committee.

(i) Approval of earmarking / cancellation of earmarking of an
accommodation to a department / institution shall be granted by the
Chief Minister.
(ii) Appeal against the order of the Chairman may be made to the House
Allotment Committee which may allow the consideration, pass such
order as it may deem fit.

7. PROCEDURE FOR ALLOTMENT.

(1) A Government Servant eligible for allotment of residential
accommodation under these rules, if so desires, may make an
application on prescribed form for the allotment of residential
accommodation to the Estate Officer through his Administrative
Department. The application received directly in the name of
Chairman House Allotment Committee shall be entertained.
(2) Applications received under rule 7(1) shall be entertained by
the Estate Officer and the names of the applicants shall be entered
in the appropriate waiting list, to be maintained for the purpose in
accordance with which the applications are received.
(3) Seniority of a Government Servant on the appropriate waiting list
shall be determined from:
(i) the date of entitlement to a type of accommodation, provided
that the Government Servant applies to Estate Office within
one month of his joining at Quetta or on his becoming entitled
to a higher class of accommodation due to increase of his
emoluments.
(ii) date of his application to Estate Officer in case he applies for
higher type of accommodation after one month of
joining/becoming entitled to higher class of accommodation.
(iii) if the date of entitlement of two or more Government Servants
is same, the seniority will be determined on the basis of
emoluments counted towards entitlement.
(iv) in case the emoluments are also the same for two or more
Government Servants, the seniority will be determined on the
basis of the date from which emoluments counting towards
entitlement accrued.
(v) in case they have the same seniority, then the seniority shall be
determined by the size of the family.
c. Receipt of allotment of accommodation shall be
acknowledged by Estate Office with a printed receipt serially
numbered in print, as and when it is received from the applicant.
The form of receipt is given in Annexure "B".
d. Allotment of Government residence will be made on the principle
of first come first served, based on the date of
receipt of application in Estate office in the respective category. If
the Government Servant becomes eligible in the higher category
during the time he is on the waiting list, he will be given position
on the list of requisite category on his application from the date of
his eligibility as such.
(3) Secretaries to Government, Member Board of Revenue, Judges of
High Court, Chairman of Public Service Commission and Members
of Secretariat staff and such other Government servants may be
notified by the Provincial Government for the purpose, in the matter
of which they will have the first priority, within their respective
categories. Heads of Attached Department, Superintendent Members
and other officers/officials with said Departments and officer will
have the second priority. The allotment of accommodation shall be
made to the Secretariat and non Secretariat officers/officials on a
cycle system in the fixed ratio of 2:1 i.e. out of three units available
for allotment, first two will be allotted to the Secretariat Officials and
the third one to the non Secretariat officials in order of their position

(4) A field officer in grade-17 or above who has designated house outside
Quetta should be provided accommodation in Quetta on preferential
basis, if a house is available for a particular post. However preference
may be given to officer transferred from out side the province.
(5) A quota of 3% of vacant houses may be fixed for allotment to female
Government servant.

8. OUT OF TURN ALLOTMENT

(1) A Government Servant deserving out of turn allotment shall apply to
the Estate Officer in the form given in Annexure "C".
(2) The Estate Officer shall grant a receipt to the applicant.
(3) The House Allotment Committee after consideration of the
application may either reject application or accept it.
(4) The application may be accepted where lack of accommodation
constitutes a serious threat to the life or is likely to lead to
deterioration of the health of the applicant or a member of his family
who should stay ordinarily with the applicant. The application may
also be accepted in cases where no possible alternative
accommodation is available for the family of the applicant any where
in the Province / Pakistan.
(5) The appeal against the decision of the House Allotment Committee
may be made to Secretary, Government of Balochistan, who
may pass such orders as he may deem fit.
(6) The House Allotment Committee shall state reasons in writing for
rejecting or accepting the applications.

9. OCCUPATION AND VACATION

(1). On receipt of the allotment order from the Estate Officer, an allottee
shall take over possession of the accommodation from Assistant Civil
Estate Officer, within 10 days of allotment and sign a receipt for all
fixtures and fittings.
(2) The Assistant Civil Estate Officer shall send the occupation report to
the "Estate Officer" within three days of occupation.
(3) On vacation the allottee shall hand over possession of the house to the
Assistant Civil Estate Officer and obtain a receipt thereof in duplicate
which shall include an inventory of the fixtures and fittings available

10. CANCELLATION
(1) The allotment of an accommodation to a Government servant is not
transferable. If an allottee or his family do not ordinarily reside in the
accommodation allotted to him and allows other person to live in the
house without permission of the Estate Officer, it may be deemed to
have been transferred by the allottee and the allotment shall be liable
to cancellation.
(2) If at any stage, it comes to the notice of Estate Office that there is a
personally owned accommodation in the name of an allottee or his/her
spouse, the allotment shall stand cancelled.
(3) The allottee shall pay rent at the prescribed rate regularly every
month. If he fails to pay the rent for three consecutive months, the
allotment shall stand cancelled.
(4) Exchange of accommodation between two allottees can be made with
the prior permission of the Estate Officer. If any exchange takes place
without such permission the allotment shall be liable to cancellation.
(5) Accommodation shall not be sublet by allottee nor shall it be used
for any business or profession. Provided that the Chairman House
Allotment Committee may, on a request, permit a Government
Servant or a member of his family to carry on medical practice.
An allottee may allow a relative to share accommodation with him
without any monetary gain for the period of one year without the
permission of the Estate Officer and with the permission of the Estate
Officer for a period of six months. Any breach of this rule shall lead
to cancellation of the allotment.
If it is proved that an allottee has sublet the accommodation, the
Estate Office shall, with approval of the Chairman House Allotment
Committee, cancel the allotment and report the matter to the head of
allottee for disciplinary action against him, under the
Balochistan Province Removal from Service (special power)
Ordinance 2002.
(8) The Estate Office shall report to Government the names of the
Government servant whose allotments have been cancelled in any one
month for subletting by the first week of the following month.
(9) If an allottee is found guilty of encroachment, the allotment shall be
liable to cancellation.
(10) An allottee found guilty of subletting shall be debarred from allotment
of accommodation for 3 years. Same penalty shall be imposed on
those who are found guilty of encroachments.
(11) The first informant of subletting case/deflection of accommodation
after ceasing of the entitlement shall be rewarded by allotment of that
particular accommodation on vacation by the allottee.

(1) in the event of death of an allottee the accommodation shall be
vacated by the widow of the allottee on the expiry of "IDDAT" period
i.e. four (04) months. In case there is no widow, the family of the
deceased shall vacate the accommodation after expiry of two months.
(2) In the event of dismissal, removal, resignation, transfer, deputation
and retirement the accommodation shall be vacated within two
months of the event.
(3) If immediate retention of the accommodation is required for the
completion of education of children in the event of death,
dismissal, removal/resignation, retirement or transfer of an allottee,
permission may be granted to retain the accommodation in payment
of normal rent for four months or till 31st December, whichever is
earlier, at the discretion of House Allotment Committee.
(4) Allotment of accommodation may be transferred to the
father/mother/rent/brother/sister/son or daughter of the
allottee, if he/she is eligible for the same or for a higher type of
accommodation at the time of the event or becomes eligible within
two months of the event and the beneficiary had been ordinarily
residing with the allottee. In case he/she is entitled to a lower class
accommodation, he/she shall be allotted the first available quarter in
that class. Till such time an alternative accommodation is made
available, he/she may retain the accommodation in continued occupation
on payment of normal rent.
(5) An allottee proceeding on leave preparatory to retirement may retain
residential accommodation for the whole period of leave preparatory
to retirement and two months beyond.
(6) An allottee, transferred to an area directed as non-family area by

12. RENT RATE & PROCEDURE FOR RECOVERY.
(1) Unless entitled to a free accommodation, the rent of accommodation
allotted to a Government servant shall be payable at 5% of his
emoluments, as defined under rule 27(1), or at such rate as
Government may specify from time to time.
(2) In case of unauthorized occupation/retention of Government
accommodation, penal rent shall be charged which may be
ten times of the normal rent. Such occupant may also be ejected
forcibly.
(3) The Rent Branch of the Maintenance Division of Communication &
Works Department shall send rent demand statements in duplicate to
the department/officers concerned and copy to the comptroller by
the 15th of each month regarding rent to be recovered from the
Gazetted and Non Gazetted servants.
(4) It shall be the responsibility of the department/officers concerned to
recover rent as per the demand statement from the Non-Gazetted staff
and the Accountant General shall be responsible for the recovery of
the Gazetted Officers. Department/officers concerned shall
report to the Estate Office as well as the Rent Branch of the
Maintenance Division the factual position of the recovery by posting
the amount recovered in the demands statement and return them to the
Estate Office and Maintenance Division by the 15th of next month.
(5) If any amount is not recovered by the Estate Office, that office shall
refer the matter to the Accountant General for recovery of the amount
under the rules who shall realize the amount accordingly and shall
not defer the realization on any appeal from the allottee concerned. If
any appeal is made to the Accountant General, that office may refer
the matter to the Estate Office for recovery.
(6) If a Government Servant for any reason does not receive pay for
certain period or periods, the rent becoming due shall be deducted
Scanned with CamScanner

from the pay bills of Government Servant concerned as and when he
gets pay for the period or periods for which the rent has not been paid,
or may be recovered in such other manner as may be permissible
under any law, rules, order, or instructions for the time being in force.
(7) Other charges such as electricity, Sui Gas, Water conservancy etc.
shall be paid directly by the allottee to the relevant Authorities.

13. NO DEMAND CERTIFICATE.

(1) The Rent Branch (Maintenance Division) Communication and Works
Department shall issue a No Demand Certificate to every allottee of
accommodation within two months of the expiry of each calendar
year.
(2) When a Government servant is transferred/retired/dismissed and
vacates the accommodation allotted to him, Estate Office and Rent
Branch or the Maintenance Division, Communication & Works
Department shall issue the No Demand Certificate within two months
of the demand for such a certificate by allottee or from the date
when the event comes to their notice.
(3) The pension/commutation cases of a Government Servant retired
from Government Service shall not be processed by Accountant
General until and unless the retiree produces No Demand Certificate
from Estate Office and C&W Department.
(4) While allotting an accommodation to a Government servant, the Civil
Estate Office shall ascertain from the Government servant about the
accommodation he was occupying in his former post, and if so
happens that he occupied an accommodation previously, Estate Office
shall ask him to file a "No Demand Certificate" in respect of previous
accommodation. In case he is unable to do so, Estate Office shall
make a reference to the Rent Branch (Maintenance Division)
Communication & and Works Department for the certificate.
However, the allotment of accommodation shall not be held-up on
this account.

14. SAVINGS.

These rules shall be in addition to and not in derogation of any instructions or
order issued by Government from time to time which hereafter be issued.

15. REPEAL.

(1) The Residential Accommodation at Quetta (Procedure for Allotment)
Rules, 1982 are hereby repealed.
(2) Notwithstanding anything contained in these rules, all allotments
made, orders passed, proceedings conducted and actions taken
under the Rules repealed in sub-rule (1) shall be deemed to have been
validly done, made, passed, conducted and taken, as if the rule was
in force on the day on which such thing, action or order was done,
taken or made.

GOVERNMENT OF BALOCHISTAN
FINANCE DEPARTMENT
(Regulation)
Dated Quetta, the 12th March, 2016.

NOTIFICATION
No.PD-SO-2016/1126/655-656. In exercise of the powers conferred under Rule 4(1) Rule 5(1)(c) read
with Rule 2(c), Rule 2(6) and the First Schedule to the Balochistan Contributory Pension Rules, 2025, the
Finance Department, Government of Balochistan, is pleased to issue the following instructions regarding
Employee's Contribution and Employee's Contribution into the Contributory Pension Fund:

(i) "Employer's Contribution" as defined under Rule 2(6) means "the amount,
computed by multiplying the employee's personable pay with the employer's
contribution rate, as specified in the First Schedule".

(ii) "Employee's Contribution" as defined under Rule 2(6) means "the amount,
computed by multiplying the employee's personable pay with the employee's
contribution rate, as specified in the First Schedule".

(iii) First Schedule- Contribution Rate:

| Head | Monthly Contribution Rate (% of pension pay) | |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| | Compulsory | Optional |
| Employee's Contribution | 12% | 9% |
| Employee's Contribution | 10% | As decided by the employee |
| Overall Contribution | 22% | |

2. However, it shall be at the discretion of an eligible employee of the Government of
Balochistan to contribute an amount exceeding the compulsory amount of 10%, based on his or her own
investment desire; in such case, the employee shall submit a duly signed affidavit/declaration to the
Finance Department, Government of Balochistan, for record and necessary action.

IMRAN ZARKOON
Finance Secretary

service: (15 days' notice)

Balochistan Rangeland Policy, 2026

1. The Balochistan Rangeland Policy, 2026

1.1 Introduction

Rangelands$^4$, some 93% of the area (Rangelands of Pakistan, current status, threats and
potential, 2016), are a vital land resource in Balochistan. According to the FAO$^5$ study (FAO, 2017),
vegetation of Balochistan Province is classified into four zones: 1) Forests (Natural Trees and
Mangroves), 2) Natural Vegetation in Wet Areas, 3) Rangelands (Natural Shrubs and Herbs), and
4) Bare Areas with Sparse Natural Vegetation. All these zones support livestock grazing,
two, i.e. Rangelands (Natural Shrubs and Herbs) and Bare Areas with Sparse Natural Vegetation,
with tree densities below 10%, could aptly be categorized as Grazing Lands$^6$, covering
approximately 64% of the province. These rangelands are further classified based on productivity
and ecology into Central Balochistan Ranges (Quetta & Bolan Divisions), Western Balochistan
Ranges (Makran Division and parts of Kalat and Rakhshan Divisions), Eastern Balochistan Ranges
(Parts of Zhob, Loralai, Sibi and Nasirabad Divisions), and the Suleiman Mountain Ranges
(Mohammad, 1989). They play a pivotal role in Balochistan's economy, providing
direct benefits such as meat, fibre, fuel, forage for livestock, and shelter for wildlife, including
migratory birds, while protecting the catchments of 19 rivers in Balochistan through
flow regulation, increased water yield, and reduced sedimentation. Indirectly, they also
contribute to environmental, health, carbon removals, recreational opportunities, and
biodiversity conservation, etc.

Rangelands in Balochistan have historically been used as communal grazing lands, with rights
determined by tribal affiliation rather than formal land ownership. Access to these grazing lands
were granted to nomadic tribes, semi-nomadic (transhumant/ seasonal migrant) tribes, or
sedentary grazers on certain agreed terms, with some even on to date. Such as, the seasonal
rights provided in exchange of livestock gift (Kebab) to tribal headman, Trini (historical border tax)
collected at some vantage point by revenue authorities, or cash/ rent to private grazing
landowner.

The main categories of rangeland tenure in Balochistan$^1$ include: 1) Tribal Claimed / Community
Owned lands; 2, Notified Forests and Protected Areas (with certain concessions/ rights of
communities, including grazing); 3, Private or individual owned; 4, Aboriginal Lands Tenure (State
owned/ Unsettled Land. In case of 4th Category, the Balochistan High Court (BHC) in a judgment
has declared that the ownership of "unsettled land" belongs to the indigenous tribes. The
"unsettled land" means the land that does not have any formal or written documents authorized
by the state. The BHC further ordered that the presumption of ownership of these unsettled lands
under Section 50(2) of the Land Revenue Act 1967 (LRA) belongs to the local tribes, and the
government is responsible for conducting the settlement records under the LRA (Sher Zaman vs
Government of Balochistan, 2018 & 2020). The matter is sub judice in Supreme Court of Pakistan.

Balochistan Rangeland Policy, 2026

Foreword

Balochistan's vast rangelands are far more than an ecological treasure; they are the mainstay of
our agro-pastoral economy, sustaining millions of livelihoods and safeguarding our biodiversity.
These vital ecosystems support livestock production, protect watersheds, act as buffer against
climate extremes, and serve as a natural safeguard against desertification. However, overgrazing,
improper management, and climate pressures have pushed these landscapes to the brink.

In a decisive response, the Government of Balochistan has launched the Balochistan Rangeland
Policy 2026, a framework to secure our environmental and economic future. This policy marks a
transformative shift toward sustainable land stewardship, prioritizing ecosystem restoration,
community-led governance, and climate-smart practices to revive degraded areas while fostering
resilience and prosperity.

This policy is aligned with Pakistan's commitments to international conventions such as the
UNCCD¹, UNCBD², and UNFCCC³, while supporting national and provincial policies, and
integrating biodiversity conservation, sustainable livestock production, and ecosystem
resilience. It embodies our pledge to harmonize ecological integrity with inclusive growth.

I extend my deepest gratitude to the European Union, experts, stakeholders, and dedicated
officials who shaped this landmark initiative. Together, let us turn this blueprint into action,
ensuring Balochistan's rangelands thrive as engines of sustainability, equity, and resilience for
generations to come.

Chief Minister Balochistan

6. Objections
(1) In response to the notice served under paragraph 5, the respondent may send his objec-
tions to the appeal by registered post acknowledgement due to the Registrar or deliver the same
to him either personally or through his Advocate one day before the date fixed for hearing of the
appeal.
(2) The objections shall be legible and concisely hand-written, type-written or printed.
shall be signed by the respondent and shall be accompanied by a copy of order or other docu-
ment on which the respondent wishes to rely in support of his objections.
(3) The written objections shall be accompanied by four spare copies thereof, complete in
all respects, and containing copies of the order and documents referred to in sub-paragraph (2).
Three of these copies shall be supplied for the use of the Tribunal and the fourth copy for the
appellant or his Advocate.
(4) In case objections are not received or delivered within the time allowed under sub-
paragraph (1), the respondent may be proceeded against ex parte.

7. Affidavits.
(1) Questions arising for determination by a Tribunal shall be decided ordinarily upon
affidavits and documents proved by affidavit but the Tribunal may direct that such questions,
as may be necessary, be decided on such other evidence and in such manner as it may
deem fit.
(2) The party affected by an affidavit may be permitted by the Tribunal to cross-examine the
deponent with reference to the statements in the affidavit.

8. Summons of witness.
(1) An application for summoning witnesses before the Tribunal shall be made, as soon as
possible, after the issue of notice of appeal under paragraph 4. It shall state -
(a) the name, designation, and address of the witness to be summoned;
(b) a brief resume of the evidence which each witness is expected to give; and
(c) a brief description of the document to be summoned and name and location the
office in which such document is expected to be.
(2) If the Tribunal is of the opinion that the evidence of any witness specified in the list of
witnesses given under sub-paragraph (1) may be of material assistance in the disposal of an
appeal before it, it shall order him to be summoned on a date to be fixed by the Tribunal; and
direct that the daily allowance and traveling charges of such witness at the rate which have
been allowed by the High Court if had summoned him shall be deposited by the person
calling him, within seven days of the date of the order.
(3) If the party filing for the summoning of a witness fails to deposit the requisite costs of
the witness within the period specified in sub-paragraph (2) or within any extension thereof
that may be granted by the Tribunal, the application on for summoning of witness, so far as
it relates to such-witness, shall be deemed to have been rejected.

13. Supply of Copy.
A copy of every order of final adjudication on an appeal shall be furnished by the
Tribunal, free of cost, to the competent authority concerned.

14. Correction of errors.
Clerical or arithmetical mistakes in an order of final adjudication, arising therein from
any accidental slip or omission may, at any time be corrected by the Tribunal either of its own
motion or on the application of any of the parties.

Provided thatwhere an application is made by a party, it shall be duly supported by
an affidavit.

15. Procedure for Inspection of Records.
The provisions contained in the High Court Rules and Orders in regard to copies
and inspection of record shall mutatis mutandis and to the extent practicable apply to the
extent practicable apply to the proceedings before a Tribunal.

16. Engagement of a Counsel by a Tribunal.
If a civil servant is un-represented before a Tribunal and cannot afford to engage a
counsel, the Tribunal may make arrangements to employ a counsel at Government expense.

Policy Preamble

Whereas it is expedient that the process of Assessment that leads individuals to
government jobs be modelled in manner that ensures transparency, meritocracy and std.
Whereas, in addition to the above, it has become an absolute necessity that the rent-seeking,
manipulative annals of the current Recruitment procedures and processes be remedied
being underpinned by Absolute Merit.
And, therefore, this Policy is practical reflection of the current Govt's stance of Absolute
Merit in as far and to the extent of securing government jobs relates.

2. Purpose and Scope

This Policy establishes a standardized, transparent, and technology enabled testing mechani-
Unit in the Chief Minister's Secretariat for recruitment in provincial government depart-
and attached entities for posts from Grade 5 and above. Recruitments conducted through
Balochistani Public Service Commission are excluded. The Policy provides a provinci-
framework to strengthen merit, ensure transparency, and streamline recruitments by addre-
bottlenecks arising from high applicant volumes and limited testing and logistical capacity. In
addition, this Unit anchors to initiate a new phase where Government Jobs will become
absolutely merit based and systemically provides the tools, ways and means through tech-
enabled landscape which eliminates zero error and human interference. This primary aim of the
Policy and thus the Unit is one such novel Governance move which the Balochistan shall be
leading in the entire public sector across the country. Nevertheless, this Policy is
inspiration and resolve from the visionary leadership of Honorable Chief Minister Balochistan
and is the practical ramification of his policy of "Absolute Merit". This Policy and thus this Unit
actuates the latter.

3. Objectives of the Policy

1. Ensure merit-based and transparent recruitments to government jobs;
2. Insulate systemically the recruitment process from manipulative practices involving
corruption, favoritism and/or nepotism;
3. Introduce automation in applications, scrutiny, and shortlisting;
4. Support departments with standardized, technology enabled testing logistics;
5. Speed up recruitment timelines through defined roles, automation, and batch wise testing
at headquarters/divisional level; and,
6. Improve public confidence in recruitment through documented controls, audit trails, and
record management.

10. Test Content and Syllabus

10.1. The concerned department shall provide the approved syllabus and
samples to the Unit at least 30 days before the test.
10.2. In case there is no approved syllabus, the Department will identify the
qualifications required and as set out in the Service Rules of the post concerned.
10.3. The Unit shall develop or arrange the test questions strictly in accordance
with the approved syllabus and test blueprint, using secure and documented processes.
10.4. In case there is no approved syllabus, the Unit shall be at liberty to
standard test as per the minimum qualification requirements as per

keeping and to avoid duplication.

(f) No project/scheme shall be proposed against future cash flows.

considered e.g. construction of a building for shelter less school where positions
are already created.

digital services.
ii. To support the IT Investments and Streamline the IT
Procurement in the province.
iii. Restrict IT intervention, which involves or having
fragmented datacenter for resource optimization.
iv. Introduction of smooth procurement framework, which
could allow departments to adopt cloud model.
v. To establish trained cloud, enable workforce in the
province with regular training and upscaling.
vi. Manage carbon footprint by reducing scattered
traditional on premises data centers and promoting
carbon neutral facilities.

[illegible] MAIN PURPOSE OF THE JOB [illegible]

The position of the Commissioner is primarily responsible to facilitate and inform
taxpayers about their duties regarding taxes, enforce tax laws to generate
revenue by collecting from existing and new taxpayers including recovery of
arrears. Main duties of this position encompass generating demand and
revenue, broadening of tax base, identifying new potential taxpayers, overseeing
audits, corresponding with senior officials and monitoring taxes and collection of
arrears from defaulters, as well as monitoring taxpayers, defaulters and
increasing demand and efficiency of the department and junior officers.

[illegible] MAIN RESPONSIBILITIES AND DUTIES [illegible]

* Work towards the remaking of the BRA into a more service oriented
organization through comprehensive policies and trainings designed for
the education and facilitation of taxpayers and departmental officers in
order to develop the Board into a modern efficient entity.

* Set goals and objectives periodically for Unit, self and subordinate officers
to fulfill according to pre-determined timelines. Maintain and monitor
progress in order to ensure regular financial control of collections, audits
and arrears.

* Ensure the achievement/completion of targets as set by the Authority for
revenue collection through the levy of due taxes, review of revenue losses
and recoveries as prescribed under law for Sales tax on Services,
Infrastructure Development Cess.

required to get internal as well as external information for the completion
of audit through the inspection of business premises, conducting field
visits and stock-taking whenever required.
* Work towards the creation of demand from review/audit of withholding
statements, and supervise recovery of current demand and recovery of
undisputed arrears demand of withholding taxes.
* Ensure the recovery of effective demand created within the year due to
registration of new taxpayers, enforce measures to blacklist or suspend

necessary.

for penalizing tax evaders. Target end result of collections to be over and
above current tax demand.
* Ensure timely and appropriate disposal of assigned cases received from

23. Medical Facilities. — All the Employees in the Service of the Authority and
their family will be entitled to free medical treatment and to claim reimbursement
of medical expenses as mentioned in the following regulations.

24. Reimbursement of Medical Expenses. — Expenses shall be reimbursed
for medical treatment:—

(a) to the employees and their dependents, which include—
(i) spouse,
(ii) dependent children i.e. son up to the age of 25 years and
daughter up to their marriage; and
(iii) parents
(b) all employees shall be required to furnish an undertaking to the
above effect as specified by Authority.

Entitlement for Treatment. — Employees/their dependents shall be entitled to—

(a) hospitalization for surgery and serious illness requiring indoor
hospitalized treatment;

(b) to avail treatment from any private or public sector hospital/clinic of
their choice in Balchistan and any other hospital/clinic in other sister
provinces which are on the approved list of the Government for its
civil servants;

(c) maternity related treatment two times in the entire service i.e. with
expenses not exceeding one basic salary during a calendar year. In
this respect expenses, such as normal / C-section delivery of child,
abortion and DNC, shall be included and considered as maternity
related expenses and

(d) the employees of the Authority and their eligible family members will
be entitled for outdoor treatment expenses. The Authority shall bear
the cost of outdoor medical consultation, Medicines and pathological

in consequence of such absence.

Balochistan Rangeland Policy, 2026

Issues and challenges of rangeland in Balochistan

1. Overgrazing and vegetation loss due to unregulated
livestock pressure and absence of rotational grazing systems.
2. Deforestation, land degradation and desertification caused
by soil erosion, shrub cutting, and unsustainable land use.
3. Climate change impacts, including erratic rainfall, droughts,
and increasing wildfire risks.
4. Lack of institutional coordination among Forest,
Livestock, Revenue and Rural Development departments.
5. Absence of formal grazing rights or tenure security for
nomadic and pastoral communities.
6. Minimal community involvement in planning,
decision-making, and restoration efforts.
7. Conflict over access and land rights among tribes,
migrants, and settled communities.
8. Weak enforcement of land-use regulations and
increasing illegal encroachments.
9. Lack of technical capacity and data on rangeland
health, biomass, and carrying capacity.
10. Inadequate financial support and policy frameworks
to guide sustainable rangeland management.

Livestock sector is the largest
contributor to Balochistan's
Provincial Gross Domestic
Product (PGDP), which account
for some 21.53% (Shah, 2023). It
provides livelihoods to over 75%
of rural inhabitants With an
estimated 48 million head of
livestock, the province accounts
for 42% of Pakistan's sheep
population, 24% of goats, and
51% of camels (Statistics, 2024)
making it a key player in the
national livestock economy.
Sheep and goats, adapted to
Balochistan's biophysical
environment, depend primarily
on the province's rangelands,
which cover 64% of its area and
supply 60% of livestock feed.

Seasonal grazing practices dominate, with sparse vegetation and
shrubs providing feed,
especially during dry seasons. However, overgrazing, land degradation, and climate
change have significantly reduced rangeland productivity. Supplemental feed from crop residues, such
as wheat and barley, is crucial during dry seasons. Despite this, feed shortages remain a pressing
challenge due to increasing livestock numbers and shrinking grazing areas. The rangelands
contribute 68.5% of the total value of livestock, and if managed to their full potential, they could
support up to 50 million head of livestock in Balochistan (Rangelands of Pakistan, current status,
threats and potential, 2016).

Balochistan's livestock products, including meat, wool, and milk, are in demand domestically
and internationally, particularly in Afghanistan and Iran. Yet, productivity and marketability are
hindered by drought, inadequate veterinary services, and traditional farming methods. Strategic
measures such as rangeland rehabilitation, rotational grazing systems, and introducing drought-
tolerant livestock species are vital. Furthermore, addition, including slaughterhouses, wool
processing units, and dairy plants, could further enhance the sector's economic potential. By
addressing these challenges, the livestock sector can significantly boost rural incomes, enhance
food security, and contribute to national and international markets (Shafiq, 2013).

1.2 Issues & Challenges.

1.2 Policy context and rationale

The rangelands of Balochistan are vital ecosystems that support the livelihoods of rural
communities, nomads, and pastoralists. Besides providing forage, rangeland ecosystems play a
crucial role in preserving surface and groundwater resources, supply 90% of the rural
population's energy needs through fuelwood, offer habitat and protection for wildlife, and serve
as recreational areas (Rangelands of Pakistan, current status, threats and potential, 2016).
However, these rangelands are under severe pressure from overgrazing, deforestation, climate
change, and land degradation, leading to reduced productivity and biodiversity loss.

Balochistan Rangeland Policy, 2026

This policy aims to ensure sustainable rangeland management, restore degraded areas, conserve
natural resources, and actively integrate local communities in governance. It seeks to safeguard
food security, strengthen rural livelihoods, mitigate climate change impacts, and promote
biodiversity conservation, while empowering communities to manage their natural resources
responsibly and equitably.

1.3 Stakeholder consultation and policy preparation

The Forest & Wildlife Department notified a Technical Working Group comprising representatives
from Forest & Wildlife Department and Livestock & Dairy Development Department and
members of the EU funded RBWRP-TA. This group drafted the initial policy document,
incorporating scientific principles, best practices, and aligning with provincial, national and
international commitments.

Tailored questionnaires were developed to capture feedback from stakeholders on key policy
elements. These were distributed to various stakeholder groups, ensuring inclusivity.

Policy consultative sessions were organized at divisional level to engage community
representatives, nomadic pastoralists, NGOs, and district officials. Provincial-level workshops
were held to consolidate feedback. The draft policy was posted on the Government of
Balochistan website and circulated among stakeholder departments, academia, NGOs for public
input.

Following integration of public and stakeholder feedback, the draft was legally vetted by the Law
& Parliamentary Affairs Department. It was then approved by the Provincial Cabinet and officially
launched by the Hon'ble Chief Minister of Balochistan.

1.4 Guiding principles and strategic alignment

The guiding principles are:

1. Sustainable and community-based resource management,
2. Capacity building, research and institutional coordination,
3. Biodiversity conservation and integration of climate change into rangeland management,
4. Livelihood and economic development, and
5. Equity, gender balance and protecting rights of indigenous and marginalized groups.

The Rangeland Policy for Balochistan aligns with international conventions, national and
provincial policies, and legal frameworks. Internationally, Pakistan is a signatory to conventions
such as the UNCCD, the UNCBD, and the UNFCCC (Nations, 1997). These agreements obligate
the province to sustainably manage its rangelands, enhance biodiversity, combat land
degradation, and mitigate climate impacts. Balochistan's rangelands, which cover 64% of its
area, are critical for achieving these global goals, making the policy a vital tool for compliance.
Nationally, the Rangeland Policy complements the National Food Security Policy (Pakistan,
National Food Security Policy, 2018), which emphasizes sustainable land use, biodiversity
conservation, and forest restoration. It also supports the National Climate Change Policy
(Pakistan, National Climate Change Policy, 2021) by promoting ecosystem-based adaptation and
mitigation strategies, including carbon sequestration through rangeland rehabilitation. The policy
further aligns with the National Forest Policy (Pakistan, National Forest Policy (NFP), 2017), which
underscores integrated land management, including rangelands, for environmental
sustainability and community benefits. Provincially, the policy strengthens and operationalises
the Balochistan Forest Act (2022), which outlines roles for sustainable rangeland and water shed
management. It also complements the Balochistan Livestock Policy and Strategy (2020-2030),

2.4.2 Governance, land tenure, and access rights
Land tenure would be clarified, communal rights recognized, and governance improved to reduce
conflicts, ensure legal certainty, and promote equitable access on unsettled and shared
rangelands.
Policy Measures:
- Clarify tenure and land-use rights on unsettled and communal rangelands to reduce
disputes and strengthen legal certainty.
- Formulate and enforce rangeland-specific governance rules aligned with existing land
and forest laws.
- Recognize customary rights and traditional land use practices of tribal communities and
nomadic pastoralists.
- Establish inclusive decision-making bodies involving local stakeholders, especially
gender, farmers and pastoral groups.
- Strengthen inter-departmental coordination mechanisms to align land governance
responsibilities across forest, revenue, and livestock departments.
2.4.3 Sustainable rangeland management:
The manageable rangelands$^7$ (some 30% of the grazing land) would be restored from degradation
through rotational grazing, erosion control, reseeding with native species, and invasive plant
management by applying both scientific and indigenous knowledge. Long-term forage
availability, soil conservation, watershed protection, and biodiversity preservation would be
improved to enhance ecological stability and rangeland productivity.
Policy Measures:
- Identification of the rangeland resource base in Balochistan with identification of priority
areas/ sites for interventions.
- For ecological stability, soil health and better livestock production stocking rate shall be
adjusted according to carrying capacity.
- Develop participatory range use plans implementing proper grazing systems, restoration,
erosion control, invasive species management, and regulate livestock for appropriate
range use.
- Avoid harmful livestock-wildlife interactions by integrating ecological knowledge and
habitat management practices into rangeland planning, ensuring spatial separation and
minimizing competition for key resources.
2.4.4 Enhancement of livestock-based livelihoods:
Recognizing that rangeland degradation undermines the productivity of the meat and wool
sectors, rangeland productivity would be enhanced to boost food security and rural incomes by
introducing drought-tolerant forage species and improving water availability to support livestock
health and productivity. Women and pastoralists would be engaged through targeted training and
capacity building to promote their active role in sustainable rangeland management and
improved livestock practices.

Balochistan Rangeland Policy, 2026

Overview

Rangelands are a critical resource for the province's agro-pastoral economy, supporting
livestock, biodiversity, and the livelihoods of millions. However, the ecosystem faces severe
challenges, including overgrazing, fuel-wood pressure, land degradation, biodiversity loss, and
the impacts of climate change. Recognizing the urgent need for sustainable management, the
Balochistan Rangeland Policy provides a comprehensive framework to restore and conserve
these vital landscapes while ensuring socio-economic benefits for local communities.

The Balochistan Rangeland Policy is a step towards ecological sustainability, economic stability,
and climate resilience. It aims to balance the needs of people, livestock, and the environment,
ensuring the long-term health of Balochistan's rangelands and their contribution to the province's
economic development. This policy reflects a shared commitment to safeguarding natural
resources for future generations.

This policy thrust areas include community-based rangeland management involving women,
farmers and pastoralists, promoting sustainable grazing practices, rehabilitation of degraded
rangelands, enhancing water conservation, rangeland advisory services, rangeland monitoring
and strengthening institutional framework. It also emphasizes participatory approaches,
strengthening the role of local communities and stakeholders, while ensuring technical support
from government departments.

Balochistan Rangeland Policy, 2026

2. Policy Framework

2.1 Policy Statement:

A resilient and productive rangeland system in Balochistan that enhances ecosystem health,
secures sustainable livelihoods, conserves biodiversity, and strengthens climate resilience for
present and future generations.

2.2 Goal:

To protect, restore, and enhance the productivity of rangelands in Balochistan by promoting
sustainable land use practices, improving the wellbeing of communities that depend on these
resources, and contributing to environmental conservation and climate resilience.

2.3 Objectives:

1. Promote sustainable land use and restoration to enhance the long-term health, productivity,
and climate resilience of rangeland ecosystems.
2. Strengthen rangeland-based livestock systems and pastoral livelihoods through improved
productivity and climate-resilient practices.
3. Ensure equitable governance, secure land tenure and access rights, and empower
communities through participatory co-management.
4. Enhance research, data, and monitoring systems, and develop sustainable financing and
incentive mechanisms for effective rangeland management.

2.4 Policy Priority Areas:

2.4.1 Community participation and co-management

Local communities, nomadic pastoralists, and village-level institutions would be empowered to
co-manage rangeland resources through the establishment of Rangeland Management
Committees and participatory decision-making processes that respect indigenous knowledge
and customary rights. Women, as key contributors to livestock care and household resilience,
would be actively included in all stages of planning and governance. Communities would lead
efforts in planning, monitoring, and conflict resolution to ensure equitable access, strengthen
stewardship, and drive the sustainable use and conservation of rangelands.

Policy Measures:

- To empower the communities, the community led management approach shall be
adopted, wherein the community shall take lead and the government shall act as a
technical advisor or a facilitator.
- Participatory Range Use Plans shall be developed at village or district levels ensuring
through engagement of CIs and Cos, ensuring inclusion of women, farmers and
pastoralist in planning, governance, management and monitoring processes.
- Integrate indigenous knowledge into rangeland management practices.
- Support community-led monitoring systems to assess rangeland health and grazing
practices.
- Promote conflict resolution mechanisms through COs/CIs to manage disputes over
rangeland access and use.

— Launch collaborative research programs with ICARDA, PFI, ILRI, and national universities
on sustainable grazing systems.
— Pilot digital tools for community-led data collection on rangeland health, livestock
movement, and climate indicators.

3.5 Capacity development and extension

The Forest & Wildlife Department's training infrastructure would be upgraded, and a dedicated
extension wing would be established to strengthen institutional and community capacities.
Capacity-building programs on sustainable grazing, rangeland rehabilitation, biodiversity
conservation, and climate adaptation would be provided to staff, communities, and
stakeholders. Regular training sessions, technical assistance, and knowledge-sharing
workshops would equip local actors to implement best practices effectively. These efforts would
enhance community stewardship, improve service delivery, and ensure a resilient, adaptive
rangeland management system aligned with changing environmental and socio-economic
realities.

Required Actions:

— Establish a dedicated extension wing within the Forest & Wildlife Department for
rangeland advisory services.
— Develop and deliver training modules on sustainable grazing, ecosystem restoration, and
climate resilience for field staff and communities with opportunities for women, farmers
and pastoralists.
— Training of Cls/Cos in grazing planning, enforcement, and restoration monitoring.
— Conduct annual rangeland stewardship workshops at divisional and district levels.
— Provide technical toolkits and guides tailored to nomadic, semi-nomadic, and settled
pastoralist systems.
— Strengthen the capacity of Cls/COs through leadership training and participatory
governance coaching.

(2) If on the date fixed for hearing of appeal or on any subsequent date to which the hearing
may be adjourned, the appellant or his advocate is not present before the Tribunal, the Tribunal
may dismiss the appeal or, if it thinks fit, may proceed to hear the other party and decide the
same.

(3) Where an appeal has been dismissed under sub-paragraph (1) or the ex-parte proceedings
have been dismissed under sub-paragraph (2) the Tribunal may on such order as it may
deem fit restore the appeal or set aside the ex-parte order as the case may be, or allow the defaul-
ting party to rejoin the proceedings.

ACT, 2014

An Act to provide protection, preservation,
conservation, sustainable and management to the Wildlife, and

Preamble. WHEREAS the Province of Balochistan has rich
biodiversity and natural heritage, especially wildlife that has
unfortunately been degrading and depleting, mainly due to
human activities. As a result, their current and potential values
are eroding to the disadvantage of the present and future
generations;

AND WHEREAS it is expedient to provide for
protection, preservation, conservation, sustainable use and

therewith, providing for amending, consolidating and
improving the law relating to these in the manner hereinafter
appearing;

It is hereby enacted as follows:

(Protection, Preservation, Conservation and Management) Act,
2014.

(2) It extends to the whole of Balochistan except
Tribal Areas.

(3) It shall come into force at once.

(1) A clinical laboratory should have enough space to accommodate different
disciplines of pathology for safe and smooth running of laboratory work.

7. PROCEDURE FOR ALLOTMENT.

(1) A Government Servant eligible for allotment of residential accommodation under these rules, if so desires, may make an application on prescribed form for the allotment of residential accommodation to the Estate Officer through his Administrative Department. No application received directly in the name of Chairman House Allotment Committee shall be entertained.

(2) (a) Applications received under sub-rule 7(1) shall be entertained by the Estate Officer and the names of the applicants shall be entered in the appropriate waiting list, to be maintained for the purpose in the order in which the applications are received.

(b) Seniority of a Government Servant on the appropriate waiting list shall be determined from :-

(i) the date of entitlement to a type of accommodation, provided that the he Government Servant applies to Estate Office within one month of his joining at Quetta or on his becoming entitled to a higher class of accommodation due to increase of his emoluments.

(ii) date of his application to Estate Officer in case he applies for higher type of accommodation after one month of joining/becoming entitled to higher class of accommodation.

(iii) if the date of entitlement of two or more Government Servants is same, the seniority will be awarded on the basis of emoluments counted towards entitlement.

(iv) in case the emoluments are also the same for two or more Government Servants, the seniority will be determined on the basis of the dates from which emoluments counting towards entitlement accrued.

(v) in case they have the same seniority, then the seniority shall be determined by the size of the family.

c. Receipt of application form for accommodation shall be acknowledged by Estate Office with a printed receipt serially numbered in print, as and when it is received from the applicant. The form of receipt is given in Annexure “B”.

d. Allotment of Government residence will be made on the principle of first come first served. The priority will be based on the date of receipt of application in Estate office in the respective category. If the Government Servant becomes eligible in the higher category during the time he is on the waiting list, he will be given position on the list of requisite category on his application from the date of his eligibility as such.

(3) Secretaries to Government, Member Board of Revenue, Judges of High Court, Chairman of Public Service Commission and Members of Secretariat staff and such other Government Servant as may be notified by the Provincial Government for the purpose, in the matter of allotment will have the first priority, within their respective categories. Heads of Attached Department, Superintendent Members and other officers/officials with said Departments and officer will have the second priority. The allotment of accommodation shall be made to the Secretariat and non Secretariat officers/officials on a cycle system in the fixed ratio of 2:1 i.e. out of three units available for allotment, first two will be allotted to the Secretariat Officials and the third one to the non Secretariat officials in order of their position

(1) The Rent Branch (Maintenance Division) Communication and Works Department shall issue a No Demand Certificate to every allottee of accommodation within two months of the expiry of each calendar year.

10. CANCELLATION
(1) The allotment of an accommodation to a Government servant is not transferable. If an allottee or his family do not ordinarily reside in the accommodation allotted to him and allows other person to live in the house without permission of the Estate Officer, it may be deemed to have been transferred by the allottee and the allotment shall be liable to cancellation.
(2) If at any stage, it comes to the notice of Estate Office that there is a personally owned accommodation in the name of an allottee or his/her spouse, the allotment shall stand cancelled.
(3) The allottee shall pay rent at the prescribed rate regularly every month. If he does not pay the rent for three consecutive months, the allotment order shall stand cancelled.

8. OUT OF TURN ALLOTMENT

(1) A Government Servant deserving out of turn allotment shall apply to the Estate Officer in the form given in Annexure ‘C’.

(2) The Estate Officer shall grant a receipt to the applicant.

(3) The House Allotment Committee after consideration of the application may either reject the application or accept it.

(4) The application may be accepted where lack of accommodation constitutes a serious threat to the life or is likely to lead to deterioration of the health of the applicant or a member of his family who should stay ordinarily with the applicant. The application may also be accepted in cases where no possible alternative accommodation is available for the family of the applicant any where in the Province / Pakistan.

The appeal against the decision of the House Allotment Committee may be made to the Chief Secretary, Government of Balochistan, who may pass such orders as he may deem fit.

(6) The House Allotment Committee shall state reasons in writing for rejecting or accepting the applications.

9. OCCUPATION AND VACATION.

(1) On receipt of the allotment order from the Estate Officer, an allottee shall take over possession of the accommodation from Assistant Civil Estate Officer, within 10 days of allotment and sign a receipt for all fixtures and fittings.

(2) The Assistant Civil Estate Officer shall send the occupation report to the ‘Estate Officer’ within three days of occupation.

(3) On vacation the allottee shall hand over possession of the house to the Assistant Civil Estate Officer and obtain a receipt thereof in duplicate which will include an inventory of the fixtures and fittings available

I. Entrance: The front of a Pharmacy shall be an inscription “Pharmacy”.

The premesis shall be built dry, well lit and ventilated and shall of sufficient dimensions to allow the good in stock, especially drugs and poison to be kept in a clearly visible and appropriate manner. The area of the Section to be used at dispensing department shall not be less than 6 sq Meters for one person working therein with additional 2 sq Meters for each additional person. The height of the premesis shall at least be 2.5 sq Meters.
The floor of the pharmacy shall be smooth and washable. The walls shall be plastered or tiled or oil painted so as to maintain smooth durable and washable surface devoid of holes cracks and cervices.
A Pharmacy shall be provided with good quality of water. The dispensing department shall be separated by a barrier to prevent the entry of public.
A Pharmacy shall be equipped with fire extinguisher to handle any emergency in case of fire.
III.Furniture & Apparatus: The furniture and apparatus of the Pharmacy shall be adopted to the uses for which they are intended and correspond to the size and requirement of the establishment.
The drugs and chemicals shall be kept in a room appropriate to their properties and in such special containers as will prevent any deterioration of contents of containers kept near them. Drawer glasses and other container used for keeping medicaments shall be of suitable size and capable of being closed tightly to prevent the entry of dust.
Every container shall bear label appropriate size, easily readable, with names of medicaments as given in Pharmacopoeias.
A Pharmacy shall be provided with a dispensing bench, the top of which shall be covered with washable and impervious material like stainless steel, laminated or plastics etc.

No. 23-10 / 73-SOI (S&GAD). In exercise of the power conferred by section 7 of the Baluchistan Tribunal Act, 1974 (Baluchistan Act No. V of 1974), the Government of Baluchistan is pleased to make the following rules namely :-
1. Short title, Commencement and Application.
(1) These rules may be called the Baluchistan Service Tribunal Rules, 1974.
(2) They shall come in-to force at once.
2. Constitution of Bench.
(1) The Chairman of a Tribunal may constitute a Single or a Division Bench of the Tribunal for hearing of appeals under the said Act.
(2) The conclusions arrived at after hearing an appeal under sub-rule (1) by a Single Bench, or as the case may be, by a Division Bench, alongwith the records of the appeal and written arguments, if any, shall be considered by the Tribunal as a whole and the decision shall be expressed in the terms of the views of the majority.
(3) The Chairman may at any stage transfer cases from one Bench to another Bench or to the whole Tribunal.
3. Procedure.
(1) The Tribunal and its Benches shall conduct business in accordance with the following procedure and every memorandum of appeal shall-
(a) be legibly, correctly and concisely handwritten, type-written or printed.

(2) The notice to the respondent shall be accompanied by a copy of memorandum of appeal and copies of other documents referred to in sub-paragraph (e) of paragraph 1.
(3) Service of notice in accordance with the provisions of this paragraph shall be deemed to be due notice, and it shall not be necessary to prove that a party has actually received the notice.
6. Objections
(1) In response to the notice served under paragraph 5, the respondent may send his objections to the appeal by registered post acknowledgement due to the Registrar or deliver the same to him either personally or through his Advocate on or before the date fixed for hearing of the appeal.
(2) The objections shall be legibly and concisely hand-written, type-written or printed, shall be signed by the respondent and shall be accompanied by a copy of the order or other document on which the respondent wishes to rely in support of his objections.
(3) The written objections shall be accompanied by four spare copies thereof, complete in all respects, and containing copies of the order and documents referred to in sub-paragraph (2). Three of those copies shall be supplied for the use of the Tribunal and the fourth copy for the appellant or his Advocate.
(4) In case objections are not received or delivered within the time allowed under sub-paragraph (1), the respondent may be proceeded against ex parte.
7. Affidavits.
(1) Questions arising for determination by a Tribunal shall be decided ordinarily upon affidavits and documents proved by affidavits but the Tribunal may direct that such questions, as it may consider necessary, be decided on such other evidence and in such manner as it may deem fit.
(2) The party affected by an affidavit may be permitted by the Tribunal to cross-examine the deponent with reference to the statements in the affidavit.
8. Summons of witness.
(1) An application for summoning witnesses before the Tribunal shall be made, as soon as possible, after the issue of notice of appeal under paragraph 4. If shall state -
(a) the name, designation, and address of the witnesses to be summoned;
(b) a brief resume of the evidence which each witness as expected to give; and
(c) a brief description of the document to the summoned and name and location the office in which such document is expected to be.
(2) If the Tribunal is of the opinion that the evidence of any witness specified in the list of witnesses given under sub-paragraph (1) may be of material assistance in the disposal of an appeal before it, it shall direct him to be summoned on a date to be fixed by the Tribunal and direct that the daily allowance and travelling charges of such witness at the rate which would have been allowed by the High Court if it had summoned him should be deposited by the person calling him, within seven days of the date of the order.
(3) If a person a plying for the summoning of a witness fails to deposit the requisite costs of the witness within the period specified in sub-paragraph (2) or within any extension thereof that may be granted by the Tribunal, the application on for summoning of witness, so far as it relates to such witness, shall be deemed to have been rejected.

(1) Evidence of a witness examined by the Tribunal shall be taken down under the superintendence of the Tribunal ordinarily in the form of a narrative and shall be signed by the members of the Tribunal and shall form part of the records.

(3) The Tribunal may record such remarks as it thinks metterial respecting the demeanour of any witness while under examination.

(4) The Tribunal may close the evidence of any party if there is inordinate delay or expense involved in its production, provided that the interest of justice so permits.

12. Ex-parte proceedings and Dismissal of Appeals.

(1) If on the date fixed for hearing of appeal or on an subsequent date to which hearing may by adjourned the respondent or any one or more of the respondents, in case there are more than one respondents, or his or their Advocates, are not present before the Tribunal, the Tribunal may hear the appeal ex-parte against all or any of the respondents.

(2) If on the date fixed for hearing of appeal or on any subsequent date to which the hearing may be adjourned, the appellant or his advocate is not present before the Tribunal, the Tribunal may dismiss the appeal or, if it thinks fit.may proceed to hear the other party and decide the same.

(3) Where an appeal has been dismissed under sub-paragraph (1) or the exparte proceedings have been taken under sub-paragraph (2) the Tribunal may on such order as to costs, as it may deem fit restore the appeal or set aside the ex-parte order as the case may be, or allow the defaulting party to rejoin the proceedings.

10. Test Content and Syllabus
10.1. The concerned department shall provide the approved syllabus and samples to the Unit at least 30 days before the test.
10.2. In case there is no approved syllabus, the Department will identify the qualifications required and as set out in the Service Rules of the post concerned.
10.3. The Unit shall develop or arrange the test questions strictly in accordance with the approved syllabus and test blueprint, using secure and documented processes.
10.4. In case there is no approved syllabus, the Unit shall be at liberty to conduct a standard test as per the minimum qualification requirements as set out in the Service Rules.
10.5. The Unit shall ensure secure creation, storage, uploading, and controlled access of test content using role-based access controls and audit logs.
10.6. The Unit shall ensure appropriate controls for confidentiality, including restricted access, secure custody, and documented handling procedures.
10.7. Where required, the department may nominate subject experts to validate the alignment of test content with the syllabus and blueprint, without compromising confidentiality.

11. Results and Post Test Process
11.1. Test results will be automatically displayed to candidates on the application portal immediately upon completion of the test.
11.2. The Unit shall not issue appointment recommendations; however, it shall generate and share merit-based lists of highest ranked candidates, including divisional wise ranking and quota wise allocation, in accordance with the prevailing rules and notified criteria.
11.3. The department concerned shall finalize Recruitment Committee proceedings, approve merit lists, and issue appointment orders as per applicable rules and procedures.
11.4. The department shall maintain official minutes and records of approvals and shall provide copies of final merit lists to the Unit for record continuity.
11.5. Result transmission shall include attendance data, session logs, and any incident reports provided by the department for context.

12. Transparency, Audit, and Record Management
The Unit shall maintain digital records of:
12.1. Applications and supporting uploads as submitted
12.2. Automated scrutiny outputs and shortlisting criteria configured for the recruitment
12.3. Shortlisting lists and system generated reports
12.4. Test attendance and session wise allocation

PREFACE

The Government of Balochistan is committed to promoting equitable development, social justice, and responsible governance across all sectors. The issuance of these Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) Guidelines represents a major step toward institutionalizing a transparent and coordinated framework for channeling CSR contributions toward public welfare and sustainable development.

The Guidelines provide clear procedures for the identification, approval, execution, and monitoring of CSR-funded projects, ensuring that every initiative reflects the priorities and aspirations of the people of Balochistan. They also emphasize accountability, participatory decision-making, and community ownership—key elements for ensuring that CSR activities deliver lasting social and economic impact.

I am of the firm believe that these Guidelines will strengthen collaboration among government institutions, the private sector, and development partners, and will serve as a valuable tool in advancing the province's development agenda.

8. SAFETY PRECAUTIONS AND MEASURES IN A CLINICAL LABORATORY:
(1) All laboratory members shall be vaccinated against infectious diseases (i.e Hepatitis-B etc).
(2) All laboratory staff must use disposable gloves and overall while performing laboratory tests.
(3) Laboratory members shall be informed on periodical basis, the hazards of handling samples working in laboratory and precautions to be taken.
(4) Laboratory staff shall ensure for safe disposal of infectious waste and refuse according to manual guidelines.
(5) Laboratory staff must be trained, how to use first aid kits, fire extinguisher and other procedures in case of laboratory incidents/accidents.
(6) All the incidents/accidents happened in laboratory shall be entered in a register mention the nature of incidents and measures taken with name of affectees, time and date of incident. A special register shall be maintained for the purpose.
(7) All the syringes/lancets must be destroyed before proper disposal.
9. UNIFORM COST OF CLINICAL TESTS:
The authority shall regulate the cost of tests. Authority shall prescribe a uniform rate list after going through the rates of provincial and other laboratories of country in such a manner which is mutually beneficial and provider of such

3.
GENERAL PROVISIONS:
(1) Authority may undertake all measures to ensure safety, protection and promotion of human life through a comprehensive and quality clinical laboratory services in the province and sustained development of such services to an internationally accepted standard, by regulating. The cost of these services which is mutually beneficial and affordable for public and providers of such services.
(2) Every physician, medical practitioner or any person qualified to do so, will ensure that the clinical tests are under-taken by a clinical laboratory which has been duly licensed and is accredited under the ordinance.
SUPERVISION OF CLINICAL LABORATORIES:
(1) The Authority shall ensure that all clinical laboratories are being supervised by a pathologist with necessary post-graduate qualification recognized by Pakistan Medical and Dental Council (PMDC Islamabad) to practice pathology.
(2) The Authority shall also ensure that all independent clinical laboratories or attached with private hospitals, clinics or any other setups, supervised by a clinical pathologist. Pathologists must be present physically in laboratories during routine working hours.
(3) In case of non availability of pathologist, private hospitals clinics and other setups shall get their investigations done from an accredited laboratory.
(4) A pathologist shall supervise one clinical laboratory at a time.
(5) In remote areas where pathologist is not available in case of emergency or a special situation where question of saving injury to a human life occurs and an accredited laboratory is not available, clinical tests may be performed by a laboratory not accredited to under take such test in a manner prescribed under the rules.
(6) Authority shall check and ensure that non medical person may not operate the clinical laboratories. Only the medical doctors who have been trained and qualified in the relevant field should be allowed to establish and operate the clinical laboratories.
(7) Technologists, technicians and laboratory assistants (duly qualified) will assist pathologists. However in remote areas of province, where pathologists are not available, they shall perform such laboratory tests under the permission of authority till the availability of a pathologist.

10. UNIFORM REPORTING SYSTEM:
The Authority shall prescribe a uniform reporting system for professional services performed.
11. RECORD KEEPING:
(1) Clinical laboratories shall maintain a proper record of test findings so that it could be used to study the prevalence of different diseases in different areas of province.
(2) Clinical laboratory shall not disclose the results of any patient to anybody in any case, until the patient himself allows to disclose the results to his attendants or relatives.
(3) Record of accounts shall also be maintained for annual report.
12. QUALITY CONTROL AND QUALITY ASSURANCE OF CLINICAL TESTS: There shall be,-
(1) A system of indoor and outdoor quality control shall be established on regular basis.
(2) Quality control sera shall regularly be used to evaluate quality of laboratory reagents and instruments.
(3) Regular service of all equipments/instruments shall be ensured on regular basis to keep such items in good working condition.
13. APPLICATION FOR REGISTRATION AND GRANT OF LICENCE:
(1) All applications for grant of a licence shall contain such information on a format prescribed by the authority.
(2) After commencement of these rules, a grace period of six months or as may be determined by authority will be allowed for all clinical laboratories to be registered with and obtain a valid licence from the authority, after which no clinical laboratory shall work without licence.
(3) Any person, hospital or clinic intending to establish a laboratory shall make an application to the authority on a prescribed form accompanied with such documents and fee as fixed by authority with the approval of Government.
14. PROCEEDINGS FOR REGISTRATION /LICENCE:
(1) The authority may on receipt of an application under rule 13, Constitute an accreditation committee to make enquiry if the clinical laboratory fulfills and complies with the terms and conditions mentioned in the Ordinance and in respect of such other matters as may be specified by it.
(2) The committee shall submit its report to the authority within a fortnight of the receipt of application or in an extended period duly approved by the Chairman.

This exercise shall be allowed only for one year. After that only those laboratory workers shall be allowed to work who will produce their certificates/diplomas from a recognized institution.
5. MANPOWER/STAFF IN A CLINICAL LABORATORY:
All clinical laboratory must be equipped with the following staff:-
(a) Pathologist (qualified) FCPS or MRCP or M.Phil or DCP or MCPS in Pathology
(b) B.S.C Technologist having matriculation or intermediate and diploma of technician or
(c) Laboratory Assistant having matriculation and diploma of laboratory assistant.
(d) Laboratory Attendants, responsible for general cleanliness of laboratory premises, washing of glassware and safe disposal of laboratory waste and refuse.
(e) Computer Operator or typist or receptionist to keep the record, typing of reports, delivery of reports etc.
Note:- Number of staff shall be according to workload of a clinical laboratory.
6. GENERAL OUT LOOK OF A CLINICAL LABORATORY:
(1) A clinical laboratory should have enough space to accommodate different disciplines of pathology for safe and smooth running of laboratory work.
(2) A clinical laboratory should be well lighted, well ventilated and clean.
(3) Room temperature of a clinical laboratory must be very comfortable to get high quality results.
(4) A laboratory should have a separate area for sample collection, reception, waiting room, and a very hygienic wash room. Patients and attendants shall not enter in laboratory working area!
